# Design decisions

Accepted architecture and policy decisions for Bob, generated from the decisions memory web.

## Answering A Walk Landing Advances The Walk {#answering-advances-the-walk}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [A Task Move Never Advances The Walk](#task-move-never-advances-the-walk)

A gesture that started on the row ]s just landed on, and whose committed write takes that row out of today's walk, advances the walk exactly once to the next remaining review item: Ctrl+Enter close, Ctrl+Alt+F, Alt+N, the Ctrl+Shift+Enter link, a resolving Task Card commit, and Ctrl+Shift+M. Alt+F is the one stay answer; Ctrl+Enter never crosses the PRE/POST boundary; a short gesture lock swallows double presses; every walk landing records a <C-o> jump.

**Applies to.** bob-plugins (bob-navigation-hotkeys, task-status-cycler,
block-id-prompt, bob-ledger-tools), bob-cli docs, the Bob vault review
ritual.

**Claim.** On the row `]s` just landed on, a gesture whose committed write
takes that row out of today's walk advances once to the next remaining item.
That covers the Ctrl+Enter close, Ctrl+Alt+F, the Alt+N commit/release, the
Ctrl+Shift+Enter link, a resolving Task Card commit, and Ctrl+Shift+M (which
advances instead of focusing the destination). Alt+F is the one stay answer.
Ctrl+Enter never auto-advances across the PRE/POST checklist boundary.
Esc, refusals, no-op writes, unlink, reopen, Reword, status cycling, and
anything off a landing stay. A short gesture lock swallows double presses
(~350 ms settle window after each advance). Every walk landing records a
`<C-o>` jump back to the answered row. Each advance shows one toast (what
was done, then where the walk landed); Task Card commits keep their rich
notice cards with the landing following on its own.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Binding each key to "action, then `]s`".** A blind second step jumps
  from the post-write cursor, skipping rows after line-shifting writes;
  anchor-only planning never does.
- **A passive queue watcher.** Reacting to any write that drops a row
  cannot tell an answer from a daytime edit and would advance off-landing
  work.
- **A second advance chord per gesture.** One more key to learn per answer
  instead of zero; the stay answer (Alt+F) already covers the opt-out.
- **A global review-mode toggle.** A mode to enter, forget, and leave in
  the wrong state; the landing scope already gates every key.
- **A dedicated triage card.** A new surface for decisions the existing
  gestures already make.
- **Nav performing every write.** Every writer keeps its own write path;
  nav only judges the outcome through capture/continue.
- **Ctrl+Enter crossing the checklist boundary.** One habitual extra press
  would close a real commitment and move away from it; Ctrl+Alt+F still
  crosses.
- **A config kill switch.** Alt+F, `<C-o>`, and a plugin rollback are
  enough.

Evidence:
`research:202610/review_walk_answer_auto_advance/review_walk_answer_auto_advance.md`;
`plan:202610/review_walk_answer_auto_advance.md`;
nav api v3 `reviewWalk` (capture/continue) in bob-navigation-hotkeys 2.6.1;
task-status-cycler 1.26.0; block-id-prompt 1.22.0; bob-ledger-tools 1.29.2;
`docs/freshness.md` §§6/13 in bob-cli.

**Cost.** A fast habitual `]s` after an answer can still skip one row once
the 350 ms window passes (`[s` or `<C-o>` recovers it); Task Card commits
show two toasts; keys are swallowed for about 350 ms after each advance.

**Reopens when.** Bryan asks for Ctrl+Enter to cross the boundary; `<C-o>`
after an answer becomes routine; the lane keep rate stays above 90%, which
questions the Alt+F / Ctrl+Alt+F pair.

Links [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](#review-walk-is-tiered) (the tier order and walk this
advance moves through).

Superseded in part: Ctrl+Shift+M only — a move never advances the walk; see
[A Task Move Never Advances The Walk](#task-move-never-advances-the-walk).

## bob-cli Releases Ride a Daily Train {#bob-cli-releases-ride-a-daily-train}

**Status:** Accepted

bob-cli ships only through the scheduled release train, at most one version per New York day after full CI on the exact SHA, with no release PR; agents never edit the Cargo.toml version or CHANGELOG.md and mark CLI or JSON contract breaks with !.

**Applies to.** bob-cli.

**Claim.** bob-cli ships only through the scheduled release train: at most one version
per New York day, and only after full CI passes on the exact SHA. There is no release
PR. Agents never edit the Cargo.toml version or CHANGELOG.md; release-plz owns both.
Agents mark CLI or JSON contract breaks with ! in the Conventional Commit subject.

**Why.** The research report
research:202610/crates_io_daily_release_train/crates_io_daily_release_train.md
compared the release-plz quickstart, a release PR with a cron merge, and a scheduled
release train. The quickstart publishes on every push; a release PR adds a merge model
and persistent review queue that this direct-to-master repository does not use; and an
hourly guarded publisher adds runs without improving the daily decision. The train
checks the exact SHA, uses the registry publication time as the live source of truth,
and rehearses in git_only mode before publishing.

The repository uses release-plz rather than cargo-semver-checks because src/lib.rs is
an internal seam rather than the product contract. cargo-dist is a binary distribution
tool, not the version and changelog authority.

**Cost.** A push can race the full CI gate; the fast-forward-only version bump then
fails and waits for a retry slot. A release may lag master by up to one day, while
Bryan's hosts and companion repositories track master. Once live, crates.io versions
are permanent, including mistakes.

**Reopens when.** The repository moves to pull requests; crates.io has no outside users
after one month of live releases; or the package size limit forces embedded assets into
a separate crate.

## Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites {#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps}

**Status:** Accepted

Typing an existing-task capture link on a task Blocked only by its own open prerequisites drops those links and then performs the gesture; plugins keep today's consumption.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, Bob Mac Capture.

**Claim.** When a capture existing-task link gesture (`@route:id` /
`^route:id`, `@route+id!`, Ensure Next `@route+id[#name]`, or
`@route:id=x…`) targets a task that is Blocked only by its own open
prerequisites (optionally plus its own single future `scheduled`),
capture removes those open prerequisite links from the managed
Depends-On line and `[dependsOn::]` field, then performs the gesture.
The drop runs only when every gate holds: a `local_dependency` reason;
no project or inherited project reason; a target other than a
recognised project's `^prj`; at most the single-field future schedule
that pull-forward already retires; exactly one accepted managed
Depends-On child; an unchanged task line between assessment and write;
and the drop staged in the same batch as the rest of the gesture. Bob
Mac Capture only renders bob's `dropped_dependencies` and `link_guard`
fields. Plugin gestures (Ctrl+Shift+Enter, `^^`) keep PDG1
consumption. `docs/task-dependencies.md` §13.5.1 owns the contract.
See also [Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line) and
[Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line](#task-deps-are-depends-on-links).

**Why.** Bryan asked on 2026-10-13 that when an `@file:id` link
gesture in `bob capture` or Bob Mac Capture targets a Blocked task
with open dependencies, capture "remove the dependency and complete
the operation when it is safe to do so. I think we always fail to do
anything currently." Consumption left the target unlinked in both
clients and read as a failure. Rejected alternatives:

- **Keep consumption.** The gesture still looks like it did nothing.
- **Drop for every reason, including project and `^prj` reasons.**
  Project prerequisites belong to the Task Card's subtree pass; dropping
  a resident's own links would not unblock it.
- **An opt-in sigil.** The live preview already shows the drop before
  submit.
- **Strike dropped links as history.** The writer form forbids strikes;
  vault git keeps the history.
- **Plugin parity in the same change.** Ctrl+Shift+Enter and `^^` stay
  on PDG1.

Evidence: `plan:202610/capture_link_drops_blocking_deps.md`; bob-cli
`92515f1` (cli-core), `bdfc8c3` (cli-gestures); bob-mac-capture
`8f89423` (mac).

**Cost.** Dropped edges leave no trace on the task beyond capture
output and vault git. Capture and plugins diverge. Project-blocked and
`^prj` targets still refuse.

**Reopens when.** Bryan wants plugin gestures to drop too; he wants a
`^prj` drop through the subtree pass; or dropped edges need a record
on the task.

## Capture `*` Blocks Existing Tasks {#capture-star-blocks-existing-tasks}

**Status:** Accepted

Capture `*` makes the new task a prerequisite of an existing task.

**Applies to.** bob-cli and Bob Mac Capture.

**Claim.** A whitespace-delimited `*note:block-id` capture modifier means
that the new or explicitly selected task blocks the named existing task.
The edge is stored only on the target task's managed Depends-On line;
the new task's BLOCKS line is its generated mirror. `*` is recognized only
in the documented leading and trailing modifier runs, with guards for
Markdown emphasis, list markers, multiplication, park operators, and
escaped literals. A bare `*` opens completion only as the final token after
other text on the same line. Capture consumes the target's live Task Links
by resolved path and block ID, preserves authored child notes as plain text,
and deletes only Pomodoro entries this capture empties. It reports consumed
links and removed entries. A newly captured blocker inherits the target's
commitment up to Next; it is linked before the target's Task Links are
consumed. Existing owners and `&` plus `*` on one item are supported.
Capture never auto-links the new task into the target's Pomodoro.

**Why.** The prerequisite is often discovered while its blocked task is
already in view, so a two-item draft and hand-invented block ID add avoidable
steps and cannot reach nested notes. `*` is the direct visual dual of `&`,
and the existing Depends-On writer can retain the single-line source of
truth. Rejected alternatives were a Task Card follow-up, directional `&`, a
`blocks:` keyword, a Mac-only toggle, authoring BLOCKS as source data,
automatic linking into the target's vacated slot, and other sigils. The
picker and preview remain renderers of bob's parse, completion, and capture
contracts.

**Cost.** Capture can edit a task note and today's ledger that the user did
not name directly, including deleting a running Pomodoro when its last link
is consumed. Capture's preservation behavior intentionally differs from
reconcile and plugin PDL7 behavior. The block is soft: a later capture link
gesture can drop it. Bob and Bob Mac Capture ship on separate release trains.

**Reopens when.** Bryan changes the `*` grammar or direction, asks for
automatic linking into the target's session, wants reconcile or plugin
consumption to preserve notes the same way, or replaces the Depends-On line
as the source of truth.

**Evidence.** `research:202610/capture_star_blocks_modifier/capture_star_blocks_modifier.md`;
`plan:202610/capture_star_blocks.md`; bob-cli commits `04a6e84` (contract),
`1a074c6` (consumption), `8774e89` (parser), `158d6de` (writer),
`78f1a69` (completion), and `1b9d35f` (execution); Bob Mac Capture commit
`f2a5cb5` (direction-aware picker and preview); publish phase `bob-cli-7n.8`.
See also [Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line](#task-deps-are-depends-on-links) and
[Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites](#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps).

## Code Copy Reads bob's Render-Time Catalog {#code-copy-reads-render-time-catalog}

**Status:** Accepted

bob records code blocks and page anchors during PDF rendering, and serves the catalog through bob ref code; clients present those bytes and never extract code from the PDF text layer or re-parse Markdown at read time.

**Applies to.** bob-cli PDF rendering and `bob ref code`, plus Bob Refs code
copy and Highlights integration.

**Claim.** Capture code and Mermaid blocks during the pandoc render that creates
the PDF. The render-time catalog records exact block text, language, attributes,
section, and anchor-derived page range, paired with the preserved source. Serve
the verified catalog through `bob ref code`; that command never runs pandoc.
Bob Mac Capture decodes bob's result, previews the payload, and copies the
reported bytes. Plain copy preserves tabs, indentation, blank lines, trailing
spaces, Unicode, and all other recorded content, with LF line endings and no
added trailing newline. Fenced copy is an explicit alternate. The PDF text layer
is only a locator during verified attachment and is never a code-copy source.

**Why.** Pandoc's render is the only point that knows which blocks reached the
PDF after transclusion, section filtering, and Mermaid conversion; it also has
the block text before PDF layout changes it and can attach page anchors. Reading
the PDF text layer silently changes code through wrapped lines, lost tabs, and
dropped glyphs. Parsing Markdown later with a second parser would disagree with
pandoc on its dialect, nested containers, and rendered block order. A shared
JSON read surface leaves one semantic authority in bob while letting the Mac
client show exactly what it will copy.

**Cost.** The catalog is derived data tied to a specific PDF and source digest,
so it must be regenerated when rendering changes and validated before use. The
Mac depends on a compatible `bob` JSON contract; clients must handle missing or
invalid catalogs without inventing fallback code.

**Reopens when.** A renderer change makes the catalog fail to match the rendered
PDF, or a future shared parser can prove exact agreement with pandoc for every
supported input route and preserve the same page and byte guarantees.

Evidence: `research:202610/ref_code_block_copy/ref_code_block_copy.md`; bob-cli
`c7ced497` (render-time catalog), `009060f9` (catalog storage), `fb28faa1`
(`bob ref code` read contract), `36ae0ef0` (verified attachment); Bob Mac
Capture `d8a828f` (catalog and picker models), `c7a5f37` (Copy card and preview
well), `7b9bbdd` (Highlights Command-Y entry).

## Decay Decisions Are Available Immediately {#decay-decisions-are-available-immediately}

**Status:** Accepted

Gesture-triggered approved-decay cards are available as soon as compatible plugins are installed; there is no calendar gate, replacement date, or counting-only period.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** Approved-decay decisions fire on an explicit Alt+F/Alt+Shift+F
gesture as soon as decay is enabled and compatible plugins are loaded
(bob-ledger-tools freshness namespace v6 with `freshnessDecayCard`
version ≥ 2). There is no October 19 switch, replacement date, opt-in,
or calendar-based counting-only period. On an exact, due Ready
ROTTEN/TICKLER task at the keep limit, a single press opens the existing
consent card and writes nothing; counted and Task Link sessions skip
those targets. A card still requires an explicit gesture, never a timer
write. `freshness.decay: false` remains the off-switch. Counting,
eligibility, explicit choices, priority/log writers, and exclusions stay
as [Rotten Keeps Decay Through The Priority Ladder](#rotten-keeps-use-priority-decay) states them.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Keep or slide the 2026-10-19 gate.** A moved constant still encodes
  obsolete policy and lets CLI, marks, and handlers disagree.
- **A replacement date, opt-in, or counting-only period.** Availability
  is immediate on a compatible install.
- **Timer-fired cards.** The card still needs a gesture.

Evidence:
`plan:202610/freshness_decay_without_trial_date_1.md`;
bob-cli `fc438bc` (`docs/freshness.md` §2a Availability, JSON schema 8
`decay {enabled, keeps, enter}`,
`tests/cli/freshness.rs::list_decides_on_early_dates`);
bob-plugins `f4b3562` (bob-ledger-tools 1.28.0, bob-navigation-hotkeys
2.2.0).

**Cost.** Mixed-version sessions stay truthful: new navigation with an
older ledger falls back to counted keeps; new ledger with older or
missing navigation shows pips without a card promise. Both languages
stay in sync under schema 8 / namespace v6.

**Reopens when.** Mixed-version fallbacks hide a needed card from a
capable install, or a future experiment needs a calendar gate.

Supersedes in part [Rotten Keeps Decay Through The Priority Ladder](#rotten-keeps-use-priority-decay) for the
activation boundary and trial-extension reopening condition only.

Amended in place 2026-10-07 at Bryan's request: the RETURNED walk tier is renamed TICKLER (machine tier `tickler`, footer label TICKS); the Ready state stays `resurfaced`.

## Event Task Links Close By The Clock {#event-task-links-close-by-the-clock}

**Status:** Accepted

Timed closes classify same-day Event Task links by meeting and session clocks; explicit picks win, except not-started events stay out of wildcard completion and parking.

**Applies to.** bob-cli and bob-plugins.

**Claim.** On a timed Pomodoro close, an unlisted plain Task Link to an Event
Task ([Event Task](../reference/glossary.md#event-task)) in the same canonical daily note is classified
by its local span and the session start `S` and close time `C`:

| Class | Rule | Default outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ended_inside` | end ≤ C and end > S | Complete and count the meeting |
| `running` | start < C < end | In Progress and carried |
| `not_started` | start ≥ C | Defer, carry, and do not count or start |
| `ended_before` | end ≤ S | Defer, carry, and do not count or start |

An explicit numbered selection wins for that link. The `!` and `*` wildcards
do not select a `not_started` Event Task; other wildcard outcomes still
apply. Ordinary Task Links, embedded links, authored `#` deferrals, and the
note-free `x0` reset keep their existing behavior.

**Why.** A plain close previously treated every linked meeting as worked,
carried it, and split the session minutes evenly. Per-meeting placeholders
still carry unselected meetings on `x` and duplicate open names are refused;
manual peeling adds repeated work to every close.

**Cost.** Rust and JavaScript must stay in lockstep through the shared
`tests/fixtures/event_task_close/vectors.json`. Back-to-back meetings in one
session still split its minutes evenly.

**Reopens when.** Same-type Pomodoro duplicates land, or meetings need
minute-level time attribution.

Evidence: `plan:202610/bob_gcal_daily_events.md`,
`docs/capture.md` § Closing the running Pomodoro,
`docs/reference/vault-format.md` § Events section and Event Tasks, and
`tests/fixtures/event_task_close/vectors.json`.

## An Empty Capture Draft Shows Today's Ledger Agenda {#idle-capture-shows-ledger-agenda}

**Status:** Accepted

An empty capture draft shows bob's `capture-pomodoros --tasks` agenda (Now, Next, Later), cached in app memory and revalidated on filtered vault events and show; folds go farthest-first (logs, one-line, one-row, name strip) below a fixed eye line; the app never reads the vault.

**Applies to.** Bob Mac Capture (agenda cache, fit planner, panel layout) and bob-cli
(`bob capture-pomodoros --tasks` as the agenda's only fact source).

**Claim.** An empty capture draft shows today's ledger agenda, painted from memory in
the first frame:

1. **bob owns every fact.** Roles, Task Link recognition, `=x`/`=` numbering, link
   resolution, task blocks, line kinds and depths, log tagging, clean titles,
   statuses, the date, and the completed summary all come from
   `bob capture-pomodoros --tasks`. See [Bob Mac Capture Is A Thin Client Of bob](#mac-capture-is-a-thin-client) and
   [Today Is Read From The Ledger, Never Written To Tasks](#today-is-read-from-the-ledger).
2. **The app owns caching, fitting, and pixels — and never reads the vault.** The last
   good snapshot lives in app memory and is revalidated on launch, on filtered vault
   events (visible `.md` notes only), on every panel show (stale-while-revalidate),
   after each submit, and on wake, unlock, and day change. Byte-identical output
   publishes nothing. A snapshot whose date is not today is never shown; a failed
   refresh keeps the last good agenda and marks it stale.
3. **Folds go farthest-first below a fixed eye line.** When the agenda does not fit,
   the farthest Pomodoros lose detail first: logs, then one-line tasks, then one row
   per Pomodoro, then the Later name strip. Next and Now fold last. Every fold leaves
   a chip naming what is hidden, and expanding a chip never moves the editor: the
   agenda is capped at the below-eye-line budget and never scrolls.
4. **Numbers match the session operators.** The current entry shows its `=x` numbers;
   every other open entry shows its `=` lineup number, because `=#NAME~K` drops by
   those same numbers. The Now countdown ticks at minute granularity while visible.

**Why.** The question Bryan most often has when opening the panel — "what am I doing,
and what's next?" — is already answered by today's ledger, so the empty draft shows
it instead of dead space, with no new concept. Caching in memory (not on disk, not in
a daemon) keeps the first frame instant on a resident app that prefetches at launch.
Farthest-first folding keeps Now fully detailed on heavy days, when recency is what
matters. The fixed eye line keeps the caret still however the agenda folds, types, or
refreshes. Rejected alternatives:

- **A daily-file cache key.** Stale-while-revalidate on filtered events is fresher
  than keying on the day file, which misses task-note edits entirely.
- **A global fold ladder.** Per-Pomodoro units with distance-ordered folding preserve
  Now; a global ladder would thin the running Pomodoro first on heavy days.
- **A horizon cap.** Dropping far Pomodoros hides actionable `=#NAME~K` numbers; the
  name strip keeps every entry reachable in one row.
- **Swift-side vault reads.** The app never parses the daily note or task notes and
  never infers current/next from the clock; every ledger judgment stays in bob.
- **Building on `bob plan`.** `plan` answers a different question (backlog order, not
  today's ledger lineup with operator numbers).
- **A fixed-height scroll list.** Scrolling moves content under a fixed caret; the
  fold ladder guarantees the agenda always fits without scrolling.

Evidence:
`research:202610/idle_capture_pomodoro_agenda/idle_capture_pomodoro_agenda.md`;
epic `bob-cli-66` (`plan:202610/idle_capture_pomodoro_agenda.md`); phases
`bob-cli-66.1` (`bob capture-pomodoros --tasks`, `docs/capture.md`, goldens),
`bob-cli-66.2` through `bob-cli-66.6` (models, store, planner, view, polish in
bob-mac-capture, CI green at `f8c9c28`).

**Cost.** One in-memory snapshot plus a background refresh per trigger; chips and
expansions add per-unit view state that resets on hide and snapshot change. The
countdown ticks only while the panel is visible. Stale marking is the only promise
when a refresh fails — yesterday's plan is never shown, but a broken link or a dead
`bob` still needs the warning rows.

**Reopens when.** The agenda needs to write the vault (row clicks, `⌘1…9` insertion),
navigate by keyboard, or show completed Pomodoros — any of which changes what the
cache must hold and what a row may do.

## Bob Mac Capture Is A Thin Client Of bob {#mac-capture-is-a-thin-client}

**Status:** Accepted

Bob Mac Capture never parses capture grammar, computes previews, or writes the vault; it runs bob, renders the spans, candidates, and previews bob returns, and submits each draft as one bob capture call.

**Applies to.** Bob Mac Capture, bob-cli.

**Claim.** bob-cli is the only implementation of capture grammar, completion data,
preview, and vault mutation. Bob Mac Capture owns presentation, process orchestration,
the global hotkey, settings, launch at login, and packaging. It spawns `bob` directly —
`capture-parse` for semantic spans, `capture-complete` for candidates and replacement
ranges, `capture --dry-run` for previews — and renders what comes back. It may filter or
rank what `bob` returned, but it never decides syntax itself; `BlockIDRules.swift` puts
it as "Bob is the only authority for the grammar". A draft is submitted as one aggregate
`bob capture`, and the panel hides only after `bob` reports success for the whole draft.
New capture behavior lands in bob-cli and `docs/capture.md` first; the app then decodes
and presents it.

**Why.** The app replaced a Hammerspoon pop-up whose `task_capture.lua` (353 lines) was
a second, independent implementation of the capture grammar in Lua. The replacement
research named that duplication — not the widget — as the root cause of the missing
completion and highlighting, and noted that any client wanting highlighting would need a
third copy. Rejected alternatives:

- **Re-implementing the grammar in Swift** — "the current pain amplified".
- **Linking bob-cli as a `staticlib` over a C ABI** — zero spawn cost, but it needs a
  stable C header and `aarch64-apple-darwin` cross-compilation.
- **A resident daemon or FFI** — judged premature: a
  `bob capture --dry-run --format json` spawn measured about 5 ms, while the old pop-up
  paid about 95 ms per stage for a login shell (both measured on athena, not the Mac).

JSON endpoints also serve any later client (a Raycast extension, an iOS Shortcut, zsh
completion) for free. Epic `bob-cli-2o` followed the rule: its bob-cli phases shipped
`plan_budget`, destination roles, the `=x` drop outcome, and `now_tag` spans, and its
two Mac phases decoded and presented them. Evidence:
`research:202608/bob_mac_capture_replacement/bob_mac_capture_replacement.md` §§2.2, 2.3,
4.2, 4.3; the Mac `README.md` opening paragraph (since `9030832`, 2026-08-13).

**Cost.** Every capture feature lands twice, bob-cli first, and the Mac half is gated by
macOS CI because agent hosts have no Swift toolchain. Every preview is a subprocess,
bounded by a 20-second timeout (`BobProcessClient.defaultTimeout`). `bob` and the app
are installed independently, so the JSON contract must grow additively: the app decodes
new fields with `decodeIfPresent` so an older `bob` still works, yet it rejects a
`schema_version` other than the one it expects.

**Reopens when.** Spawn latency measured on the Mac breaks live preview, or a second
frontend needs an in-process library. Even then exactly one semantic implementation must
remain: reopening can change the transport (a daemon, FFI), never add a second grammar.

## Note Ready Cap Counts The Lane {#note-ready-cap-counts-the-lane}

**Status:** Accepted

The per-note soft cap (plan.max_ready_per_note, default 5; ready_cap: N|off) counts each area/project note's whole Ready lane by residence, whatever its freshness.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault, dash.

**Claim.** Every area/project note has a soft cap on its Ready lane
(`plan.max_ready_per_note`, default 5; per-note `ready_cap: N|off`). The
cap counts each note's whole Ready lane by residence, whatever its
freshness. Recurring and `^prj` rows are excluded. Crowded means strictly
over; full is neutral. Nothing is refused, written, or stored. The dash
chip order becomes NEW, PENDING, NEXT, READY, CROWDED, BLOCKED, ROTTEN,
TODAY.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Gated per-note count.** Rot cliff and review inversion: skipping
  review would lower the count without lowering pressure.
- **OPEN/SHOWN vocabulary.** Crowded, full, and room stay the words.
- **Hard refusal of moves.** Crowded notes never fail the report.
- **Auto-defer or auto-split.** The fix stays split, sequence, defer,
  or drop by hand.
- **Stored counts.** Counts stay a read-time evaluation; frontmatter
  holds only the `ready_cap` override.
- **Hooks badge row.** Lane semantics stay unchanged.
- **Parent rollups.** Residence only; never parent, heading, embed,
  or backlink.
- **Separate area default.** One global key plus the per-note
  override.
- **Amber at-limit color.** Full is neutral; only crowded is red.
- **Folding into the READY chip.** CROWDED is its own chip.

Evidence:
`research:202610/per_note_ready_cap/per_note_ready_cap.md`;
`plan:202610/per_note_ready_cap.md`;
`docs/plan.md` Ready cap per note in bob-cli.

**Cost.** Per-note counts don't sum to READY; two implementations
(Rust plus JavaScript) stay in sync under vectors R1–R14; the mobile
default cap applies where `config.yml` is unreadable.

**Reopens when.** Bryan finds the cap unhelpful after tuning N and the
notice scope.

Amended in place 2026-10-04 at Bryan's request: the freshness trial was removed; nothing waits on it.

## #now Is A User-Owned Weekly Bet, Never A Status {#now-tag-is-user-owned}

**Status:** Superseded by [Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived](#task-lanes-are-sticky), [Today Is Read From The Ledger, Never Written To Tasks](#today-is-read-from-the-ledger)

Only Bryan's explicit gestures add or remove #now; no automation infers, adds, or strips it. It never changes task status or feeds Next, and it stays a tag, never an inline field.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, Bob Mac Capture, vault.

**Claim.** `#now` is a plain Obsidian tag on a `#task` line that marks one of this
week's bets. It is the Now tier of the roadmap: Now is `#now`, Next is Ready work, and
Later is a P1–P4 deferral (`p:<N>` in capture, Ctrl+Shift+P in Obsidian). Only an
explicit gesture writes it: typing it, a trailing `#now` on new capture text, or Bob
Navigation Hotkeys' Alt+N toggle and Ctrl+Shift+P `#now` row. Nothing adds it implicitly
— removing a Task Link with Ctrl+Shift+Enter or dropping one with `=x~<K>` leaves the
tag as it was — and no hook, cron job, or sync strips it. It is independent of the
checkbox: `bob task-status-hooks` only counts it, it never makes a task Next, and a task
can be both `#now` and `[/]`. The NOW cap (`plan.max_now`, default 15) is visibility,
not enforcement: over the cap, chips and `bob plan` turn red and `now_cap_exceeded` is
reported, but nothing refuses. `docs/plan.md` owns the NOW query and its Rust and
JavaScript implementations; `docs/capture.md` owns the grammar.

**Why.** The tag answers the status-lock trap measured on 2026-09-29: removing a task's
Task Link from today's [Pomodoro](../reference/glossary.md#pomodoro) ledger demoted it, and nothing else
remembered that it mattered this week, so everything stayed linked — about 50 `[/]` and
25 `[*]` tasks, and 80 queued links, 58% of them a week or more without a 🍅. A tag only
Bryan owns separates commitment from activity, so the derived statuses in
[Active Task Statuses Are Derived, Not Authored](#task-status-is-derived) can decay honestly: `[/]` is a footprint, `#now` a
promise. Rejected alternatives:

- **An inline `[roadmap:: now]` or `[horizon:: …]` field.** Bob's property writer
  appends fields at the far right, and Tasks parses trailing Dataview fields right to
  left; a scratch-vault test showed such a field silently erasing `priority` and
  `created`. A tag is safe anywhere on the line, as `#hide` already is.
- **`#now` as a Next source, or tools that backfill it.** Keeping `#now` tasks Next
  re-inflates NEXT; hooks or cron that sweep leftovers into a horizon edit history
  behind open editors and multi-machine sync; and silent diversion hides where a task
  went.
- **A hand-kept `roadmap.md`, explicit Next/Later values, or a `roadmap.base`.**
  Hand-kept horizon lists had already died twice in the vault (the zorg-era
  `now_*`/`soon_*`/`maybe_*` notes and `sase_blog_blockers.md`); P-levels already are
  the Later horizon and resurface on their own; and Bases rows are files, not tasks.
- **New capture tokens** (`h:`, `r:`, `~id`, `!id`). `#now` in body text already parsed.

Evidence:
`research:202609/pomodoro_closed_day_now_tag_automation/pomodoro_closed_day_now_tag_automation.md`
§§1, 2, 4, 6.4; `research:202609/now_tag_vs_in_progress_status.md`; epic `bob-cli-2o`
(`plan:202609/pomodoro_plan_budget_now_tag.md`); bob-cli `d28f8cd`; bob-plugins
`b68618f`.

**Cost.** A second marker with a manual lifecycle: only the Monday review prunes NOW,
and if that lapses NOW becomes the next pile with nothing but a red chip to say so.
Dropping a link never tags the task, so Bryan must tag before dropping or lose it from
view. The tag survives deferral — a P-level makes the task Blocked and hides it from
NOW, and it reappears when the date arrives unless untagged. Capture can tag only new
task text; tagging an existing task needs Obsidian. The NOW predicate is implemented in
Rust and mirrored in JavaScript, and both must keep matching the dash's query defaults.

**Reopens when.** The two-week trial (2026-09-30 → 2026-10-13) or a later weekly review
shows NOW ignored — the research's rule is then to delete the tag and keep only the
capped ledger; promotion from Ready proves too slow and a second horizon tag such as
`#next` is needed; or Obsidian Tasks or Bases gains task-level properties that are as
parser-safe as a tag.

Superseded: `#now` is retired — see [Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived](#task-lanes-are-sticky) and
[Today Is Read From The Ledger, Never Written To Tasks](#today-is-read-from-the-ledger). The Next lane now holds this week's
commitments.

## Open PDF Writes Are Coordinated {#open-pdf-writes-are-coordinated}

**Status:** Accepted

bob writes Highlights PDFs only through bounded .forMerging file coordination around the whole per-PDF write, holding when uncertain or while you read; never UI automation, never .forReplacing.

**Applies to.** bob-cli (`ref scan`, `ref sync`, create-time ingest),
Bob Mac Capture (Refs scan presentation), the vault.

**Claim.** When `highlights.coordinate_pdf_writes` is on, every Highlights
PDF marker write goes through one bounded macOS file-coordination write
(`NSFileCoordinator`, `.forMerging`, 10 s per PDF from a 30 s scan cap)
around the whole per-PDF write sequence. macOS has Highlights save your
unsaved annotations first, bob re-checks the marker in the fresh bytes and
writes on top of them, and Highlights reloads the same tab in place. Any
uncertain branch becomes a hold — `editor_active`, `coordination_timeout`,
or `marker_changed` — with nothing written for that PDF, exit 0, and a
retry on the next scan. bob never presses keys, closes or reopens tabs,
grants itself Accessibility, or falls back to an uncoordinated write;
`.forReplacing` and option-less writes are never used. Bob Mac Capture
presents refreshes and holds from bob's scan receipt, never by reading
the vault. The key ships off until the guided acceptance test
(`scripts/dev/highlights_coordination_acceptance`) passes on the Mac.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Scripted ⌘S / close / reopen of Highlights.** Keystrokes steal focus,
  need an Accessibility grant for bob, and churn tabs.
- **`.forReplacing` or option-less writes.** Both silently drop unsaved
  annotations; only `.forMerging` asks the open document to save first.
- **Defer-while-open as the primary strategy.** Waiting for Highlights to
  go idle leaves markers stale for whole reading sessions; holds stay the
  exception (reading, blocked save, changed marker), not the rule.
- **Dropping `-w` from the cron.** The cron keeps writing through
  coordination instead of going note-only.

Evidence:
`research:202610/highlights_open_pdf_coordinated_marker_writes/highlights_open_pdf_coordinated_marker_writes.md`;
`plan:202610/highlights_coordinated_marker_writes.md`;
epic `bob-cli-at` (`coordinate`, `policy`, `executor`, `report`,
`mac-core`, `mac-app`, `accept` phases).

**Cost.** Whole-PDF holds delay annotation import by at most one scan;
a coordinated reload resets the document's undo history; the shipped
default stays off until Bryan's acceptance run passes.

**Reopens when.** The real-Highlights acceptance test shows lost
annotations or a conflict dialog (then Plan B, an app-driven "Apply
now"), or a macOS upgrade breaks file coordination.

## A Pomodoro Theme Is One Name Component {#pomodoro-theme-is-one-component}

**Status:** Accepted

A theme is one + component of a Pomodoro's — NAME tail, keyed by normalize_component, with the catalog derived from canonical daily notes.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, Bob Mac Capture, the Bob vault.

**Claim.** A Pomodoro **theme** is one `+`-separated component of a named ledger
entry's ` — NAME` tail. Split with `split_components`. The key is
`normalize_component` (whitespace collapsed, lowercased). The display name is the
most recent authored spelling for that key. `— BOB + DECKS` is one Pomodoro name
with two themes. An unnamed entry, the budget's `(unnamed)` placeholder, a
Pomodoro home, and an Obsidian appearance theme are not themes. The catalog is
derived from canonical daily notes `YYYY/YYYYMMDD.md` through
`capture_pomodoros::scan`, plus the hide/color journal. `bob themes` lists it.

**Why.** Treating the whole ` — NAME` as one theme would hide composites such as
`BOB + DECKS` from per-component recency, color, and hide. Scanning task text or
homes would invent history the ledger never recorded. Rejected alternatives:

- **Whole-name identity** — `BOB + DECKS` would be a third theme beside BOB and
  DECKS, and hide/color could not target one component.
- **Slug-only keys** — `SASE V18` and `SASE-V18` would collide or split against
  the plan budget's existing `normalize_component`.
- **Inferring themes from tasks or homes** — the ledger would stop being the
  source of truth.

Evidence: `plan:202610/pomodoro_themes.md` PT1–PT2; `docs/pomodoro-themes.md`.

**Cost.** Every consumer splits names the same way. A rename rewrites one
component across tails, not a whole name. Clients must not scan the vault for
identity.

**Reopens when.** The plan budget and the catalog disagree on what a component
is, or unnamed entries need a remembered identity.

## Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line {#projects-block-from-prj-line}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Sub-projects Inherit Project Blocking](#subprojects-inherit-project-blocking), [Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites](#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps)

A project's prerequisites and date live on its ^prj task; while that line is Blocked, every open resident is Blocked and tagged #prj_is_blocked, and Blocked tasks keep no Task Links under today's open Pomodoros.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** A project's prerequisites live on its `^prj` Depends-On line
and its date as inline `[scheduled::]`, with no project frontmatter
`depends_on` or `scheduled`. While `^prj` has its own reason to be
Blocked — an open projected prerequisite, or a future inline date —
every open task in its note is Blocked `[?]` and carries the
machine-owned `#prj_is_blocked` tag. `^prj` itself is never tagged; a
hand-set `[?]` on `^prj` blocks nobody. There is no sub-project
cascade: blocking is by residence only. Blocked tasks keep no Task
Links under today's open Pomodoros: a gesture that would link one
raises its open prerequisites instead (or reports a project date), and
`bob task reconcile` removes stale live links and emptied Pomodoros.
`docs/task-dependencies.md` §13 owns the contract; see also
[Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line](#task-deps-are-depends-on-links),
[Active Task Statuses Are Derived, Not Authored](#task-status-is-derived), and
[Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived](#task-lanes-are-sticky).

**Why.** Frontmatter is not needed: no vault query reads project
`scheduled` or `depends_on`, and the `^prj` line already drives
reconcile, R1–R10, successor recovery, the Depends on stage, and
ledger chips. The project design already treats the task line as the
interaction point. Inheritance without consumption would leave Blocked
work planned today. A tag on every open resident states a fact about
the project, so writers do not recompute it when a resident's own
reasons change. Rejected alternatives:

- **Frontmatter `depends_on` / `scheduled` (canceled bob-cli-6s).** YAML
  storage was the odd one out and raced `bob-project-tasks`.
- **Inheritance without consumption.** Blocked tasks would keep live
  Task Links.
- **Copying project dependencies onto residents.** Duplicate edges and
  a second writer surface.
- **Residents depending on their own `^prj`.** A guaranteed deadlock.
- **`status: waiting` as a reason.** Status stays derived from the
  line.
- **A Blocked overlay.** Lanes do not survive Blocked.
- **A sub-project cascade.** Blocking is by residence only.
- **A render-only reason chip instead of a tag.** `blocked.md` and JS
  paths need a stored token.
- **Tag only sole-reason residents.** Every immediate writer would
  recompute the tag; `every_resident` states a project fact.

Evidence:
`research:202610/prj_task_inline_schedule_and_deps.md`;
`research:202610/project_dependency_blocking/project_dependency_blocking.md`;
epic `bob-cli-6u` (`plan:202610/prj_line_project_blocking.md`);
bob-cli `37c100f` (contract), `f6fbd7d` (cli-model), `23f2fd9` (hoist),
`34d4ab6` (reconcile block/tag), `2340689` (consume links),
`13d183f` (close), `66c4ddb` / `36f997b` (capture);
bob-plugins `c9938d8` (nav-model), `a42f45d` (schedule),
`046028c` (Depends on), `1abde2f` (convert/move), `744247c`
(cycler/block-id-prompt).

**Cost.** Lane loss is project-wide. The `^prj` line is longer. Tasks
and Dataview `tags include #prj` is a substring match for
`#prj_is_blocked`. A missed immediate tag write is repaired only on
the next reconcile. Project dates still propagate onto residents
(raise-only; a hand-edited earlier `^prj` date keeps old copies).
Consumption may delete a running timed Pomodoro. Daily-note tasks keep
the R9 carve-out.

**Reopens when.** Lanes must survive Blocked; Bryan wants a sub-project
cascade or re-linking on unblock; a projects-by-date Properties/Bases
view is needed.

Superseded in part: residence-only blocking remains for each project’s own residents; sub-project descendants now inherit blocked ancestor reasons — see [Sub-projects Inherit Project Blocking](#subprojects-inherit-project-blocking). Capture link gestures on a task blocked only by its own prerequisites now drop them and link ([Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites](#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps)).

## READY Is Freshness-Gated With NEW and ROTTEN Review {#ready-is-freshness-gated}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Note Ready Cap Counts The Lane](#note-ready-cap-counts-the-lane), [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](#review-walk-is-tiered), [Rotten Keeps Decay Through The Priority Ladder](#rotten-keeps-use-priority-decay), [Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers)

READY is the freshness-gated confirmed/exempt backlog (visible TODO pool minus NEW and ROTTEN buckets) with TODAY → NEW → PENDING → NEXT → READY sections and NEW/PENDING/NEXT/READY/BLOCKED/ROTTEN/TODAY chips; review clears NEW then ROTTEN; no tags, fields, or status changes store review state.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault, dash.

**Claim.** READY means recently human-confirmed work plus the preexisting
freshness-exempt Ready tasks, computed at read time from the stable bucket
contract in `docs/freshness.md` §4 (`bucket(new)`, `bucket(rotten)` for
resurfaced and age-expired, null otherwise). The visible pool partitions as
`B = NEW ∪ TICKLER ∪ ROTTEN ∪ READY`, pairwise disjoint. Dash section order
is TODAY → NEW → PENDING → NEXT → READY; chip order is NEW, PENDING, NEXT,
READY, BLOCKED, ROTTEN, TODAY. NEW (unconfirmed, always visible, never
limited) clears to 0 first, then `rotten.md` (TICKLER plus expired ROTTEN)
until 0 or budget, then PENDING → NEXT. Tasks stay in their source notes;
`rotten.md` rows are click-through views and `]s` / Alt+Shift+F reviews
source lines. Rejected alternatives:

- **Stored `#rotten` / `#new` tags, persisted classification, new statuses,
  task relocation, or automatic confirmation.** Classification stays a
  read-time evaluation; stamps remain the only write.
- **Duplicate inline evaluators in dash queries.** Dash and rotten share one
  snapshot-backed bucket predicate and `reviewModel()`.
- **Dim-not-hide as the initial policy.** Review buckets stay out of READY;
  dimming is reconsidered only if gating hides needed work after interval/budget tuning.
- **Filtering READY with `state === "fresh"`.** That would lose exempt tasks;
  READY uses `bucket !== "new" && bucket !== "rotten"` on the visible pool.

Evidence:
`plan:202610/freshness_gated_ready.md`;
`research:202610/freshness_gated_ready_dash/freshness_gated_ready_dash.md`;
`docs/freshness.md` §§4/6/8/13 and `docs/plan.md` READY backlog in bob-cli;
`api.freshness.bucket` plus `reviewModel()` and gated `readyBudget` in
bob-ledger-tools 1.11.0; `dash.md` NEW/gated-READY plus `rotten.md`
TICKLER/ROTTEN groups in the vault.

**Cost.** READY visibility depends on review: skipping review lowers READY
without lowering total lane pressure. Headless `bob query` without the plugin
stays ungated; `bob freshness list` is the headless review interface. Two
implementations (Rust bucket plus JavaScript bucket/model) stay in sync under
schema 1 until the vocab-rotten migration.

**Reopens when.** A required plugin-free surface needs gating, or gating hides
needed work (a lost-needed-task case) after interval/budget tuning.

Supersedes in part [Today Is Read From The Ledger, Never Written To Tasks](#today-is-read-from-the-ledger) for the dash
section list only.

Superseded in part: chip list only — see [Note Ready Cap Counts The Lane](#note-ready-cap-counts-the-lane).

Superseded in part: review ritual order only — see [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](#review-walk-is-tiered).

Amended in place 2026-10-04 at Bryan's request: the freshness trial was removed; nothing waits on it.

Superseded in part: 'stamps remain the only write' only — the approved
decision card invokes separate existing writers on explicit approval, see
[Rotten Keeps Decay Through The Priority Ladder](#rotten-keeps-use-priority-decay).

Amended in place 2026-10-07 at Bryan's request: the RETURNED walk tier is renamed TICKLER (machine tier `tickler`, footer label TICKS); the Ready state stays `resurfaced`.

Superseded in part: `[unblocked::]` is a stored input that makes a task
due, while classification stays read-time — see
[Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers).

## Recurring Occurrences Walk When Due {#recurring-occurrences-walk-when-due}

**Status:** Accepted

The ]s walk is PRE → NEW → PROJECTS → PENDING → NEXT → RECURRING → TICKLER → ROTTEN → POST; due recurring occurrences walk in RECURRING (never stamped); schema 13 retired REFERENCES so refs use ordinary groups; a ^prj walks in PROJECTS only when it lacks #hide.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** The shared freshness walk is nine tiers: PRE → NEW → PROJECTS →
PENDING → NEXT → RECURRING → TICKLER → ROTTEN → POST (`docs/freshness.md`
schema 14). A non-checklist recurring task whose occurrence date (the
earliest valid `scheduled`, `due`, or `start`) has arrived walks in
RECURRING, between NEXT and TICKLER (`tier_position=before_tickler`). It
is never stamped. It leaves the walk when completed, rescheduled past
today, linked to Today, or cancelled through Tasks. Alt+F and Ctrl+Alt+F
on a landed RECURRING row write nothing and stay (`ctrl_alt_f=refuse`);
the notice names the real answers (Ctrl+Enter, link, reschedule). Schema
13 retired the REFERENCES tier: `#ref` and legacy `^ref` tasks use
ordinary NEW, lane, TICKLER, and ROTTEN groups. `^prj` remains the only
tracker exception. A `^prj` walks in PROJECTS only when it lacks `#hide`,
which `bob projects sync` owns; there is no open-task occupancy count and
no frontmatter `scheduled` gate.

**Why.** Recurring rows were excluded from every stamp-resolved tier
because Tasks copies `[fresh::]` into the next occurrence and because
the old full-READY walk was assumed to surface them. After the due-only
walk replaced that READY walk, arrived occurrences vanished from `]s`,
the footer, and `bob freshness list` (four overdue non-checklist rows on
2026-10-08). RECURRING restores the "recurrence resurfaces it" half
without stamping. Grouping it with TICKLER keeps the date-driven arrival
tiers together and leaves NEW first after PRE. A reflexive Ctrl+Alt+F
must never mark a due obligation done. Bryan then asked that `^prj`
review follow the `#hide` tag `bob projects sync` already writes, and
that reference tasks follow the same freshness and review rules as other
tasks in their lane.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Stamping recurring rows.** Tasks copies `[fresh::]`/`[keeps::]`
  forward, and an overdue fixed-cadence completion would create an
  already-arrived occurrence that looks fresh and hides.
- **Folding the rows into TICKLER.** TICKLER resolves by stamp.
- **Walking undated recurring rows daily.** They have no occurrence; they
  get a `recurring_undated` lint instead.
- **Admitting `[?]` like checklist rows.** The 15-minute hooks restore
  `[ ]` after the date arrives; the row stays due the next morning.
- **`tier_position=after_pre`.** That would put due recurring obligations
  immediately after PRE chores and push NEW off the first post-chore
  slot.
- **`ctrl_alt_f=skip`.** Write nothing and advance like `]s`; a due
  recurring row would get no explicit answer.
- **Ctrl+Alt+F completes, as on PRE/POST.** A reflexive key must never
  mark Pay salary done.
- **Lifting the recurring exclusion for every task.** Recurring rows
  still never enter NEW or ROTTEN.
- **Keeping a REFERENCES tier and `reference_interval`.** Bryan asked
  that refs use ordinary lane freshness.
- **PROJECTS occupancy counts or a frontmatter `scheduled` gate.** Sync
  already encodes occupancy and future-schedule hiding in `#hide`.

Evidence:
`plan:202610/recurring_review_tier.md` (`tier_position=before_tickler`,
`ctrl_alt_f=refuse`);
`plan:202610/recurring_review_landing.md`;
`plan:202610/tracker_hide_gate_and_references_tier.md`;
`plan:202610/unify_reference_task_freshness.md`;
`docs/freshness.md` schema 14;
bob-cli `56a5e688` (schema 11 RECURRING), `54712fea` (`#hide` PROJECTS
gate), `87501347` (schema 13 ordinary refs);
bob-plugins `9233b0c` (ledger freshness namespace v9 `recurringTier`);
the 2026-10-08 census of four overdue recurring rows.

**Cost.** A due recurring row asks every morning until answered. An
overdue fixed-cadence task needs one answer per missed occurrence, or
one reschedule. An arrival-morning `[?]` row appears only after the
first hooks run. Hidden empty projects wait on `bob projects sync`
(every 15 minutes) before their `^prj` walks.

**Reopens when.** An arrival-morning miss is traced to a stale `[?]`, or
RECURRING rows are routinely skipped with `]s` (then they need a
snooze).

Links [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](#review-walk-is-tiered) (the older nine-tier order,
blanket recurring exclusion, and REFERENCES claim this record
supersedes in part) and [Answering A Walk Landing Advances The Walk](#answering-advances-the-walk)
(RECURRING answers stay; Ctrl+Alt+F refuses).

## Ref Rename Keeps Reference Identity {#ref-rename-keeps-identity}

**Status:** Superseded by [Reference Renames Keep Identity](#reference-renames-keep-identity)

Ref renames change bundle paths while preserving reference and task identity.

*Accepted · project*

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-mac-capture, bob-plugins.

**Claim.** `bob ref rename` changes the file stem for a modern reference bundle:
the note, PDF, sidecar, audio, and vault links to those files. It keeps the
frontmatter `id`, the reading task's `^ref` block ID, `title`, `source_url`, the
PDF marker, and the PDF bytes. V1 refuses annotated references. If annotated
renames are needed later, the pipeline will own an identity-origin frontmatter
field so it can preserve highlight IDs instead of re-keying `^h-` anchors.

**Why.** Changing `id` or `^ref` requires writing the PDF marker and churns the
Today, Task Links, and Depends-On joins. Re-keying highlights would require
rewriting anchors, assets, inbound fragments, and archived `[h::]` digests.
Matching by content would add fuzzy matching to every scan. The file stem is
therefore a locator; it is not the reference's identity.

**Cost.** The stable `id` may differ from the filename stem; six existing
references already have that shape.

**Reopens when.** An annotated reference rename is needed.

Evidence: research report
`research:202610/bob_ref_rename_command/bob_ref_rename_command.md`; epic
`bob-cli-7x` (`plan:202610/bob_ref_rename.md`); live writer and verification
phase `bob-cli-7x.4` (`docs/ref.md`, `tests/cli/ref_library/rename.rs`).

Superseded: the earlier bundle-path and task-identity claim is consolidated in [Reference Renames Keep Identity](#reference-renames-keep-identity), which records the supported scope and identity invariants.

## Reference Ids Follow File Stems {#reference-ids-follow-file-stems}

**Status:** Accepted

A reference id follows its note stem, with a numbered suffix only to avoid duplicate ids across ref/.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, Bob Mac Capture's rename card, and the Bob vault.

**Claim.** A reference's recorded `id` equals its note stem. The only exception is a
`_N` suffix that avoids a duplicate across `ref/`. `bob ref rename` re-keys the id in
frontmatter and the PDF marker with the stem; a same-stem rename repairs a mismatch.
The reading task's `^ref-…` block ID, title, `source_url`, and dates stay unchanged.
References without an id stay id-less.

**Why.** Bryan's rule is that “a reference's id, which is recorded in the PDF's
page-1 marker and in the note's frontmatter `id`, must equal the reference note's
basename. The only allowed exception is avoiding a duplicate id. Ids must be distinct
across the whole `ref/` directory.” The id is a lookup and display key; URL deduplication
uses `source_url`, so re-keying it breaks no identity join. The sync engine already
propagates a note-side id edit to the PDF marker and refreshes sync bookkeeping.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Keep the stale id.** This preserves the previous claim that rename identity lives in
  the id even though the file stem is the required id.
- **Re-key the `^ref` block ID too.** That would churn Task Links, `[id::]`, and
  Depends-On links that join on the block ID.
- **Refuse when another reference uses the stem id.** A numbered suffix preserves the
  rule and leaves every id unambiguous.

**Cost.** An id change rewrites the PDF bytes and makes `bob ref find <old id>` stop
resolving. A PDF left open in Highlights could later write back its stale marker.

**Reopens when.** Reference ids gain another consumer, or the reading-task block ID
must follow the file stem.

Evidence: `plan:202610/ref_rename_id_follows_stem.md`, `docs/ref.md`, and
`tests/cli/ref_library/rename.rs`.

## Reference Renames Keep Identity {#reference-renames-keep-identity}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Reference Ids Follow File Stems](#reference-ids-follow-file-stems)

Renaming eligible references moves their bundle paths and inbound links while preserving reference and reading-task identity.

aka bob ref rename, reference rename, preserve ref identity

**Applies to.** bob-cli, Bob Mac Capture's Bob Refs rename flow, bob-plugins, and
the Bob vault's reference links.

**Claim.** Renaming an eligible modern, PDF-backed, unannotated reference changes
its file stem and the corresponding bundle paths in the same reference-type
directory. The bundle includes the note, PDF, and any same-stem sidecar or audio
companions; the rename also rewrites inbound vault links and the note's companion
paths. It keeps the reference's `id`, `^ref-…` block ID, title, `source_url`,
dates, PDF marker, and PDF bytes. The reading task therefore retains its identity
and links. V1 refuses legacy and intake references, annotated references, and
notes whose PDF sync plan is not clean. Refiling, retitling, bulk renames, and
intake renames are outside this contract.

**Why.** The `id` is the URL deduplication key and the `^ref-…` block ID joins the
reading task to the reference. Changing either would break identity joins and
churn Today, Task Links, and Depends-On links. The file stem is a locator, not the
reference's identity; six existing references already have an ID that differs
from the filename stem. A scratch-vault experiment showed that moving the PDF
and note, rewriting inbound links, and updating only `source_pdf` lets
`bob ref sync -d <new pdf>` plan no changes while `bob ref find <old id>` still
resolves. Note-only renames can make the next scan recreate the old note and
duplicate the reading task. Re-keying highlights would require rewriting
anchors, assets, inbound fragments, and archived `[h::]` digests.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Mint a new reference ID.** That breaks URL deduplication and turns the same source
  into a second reference.
- **Change the `^ref` block ID.** That disconnects existing task links from the reading
  task.
- **Rename annotated references in this version.** Highlight IDs and follow-up digests
  depend on paths, so changing those paths would require re-keying annotations.
- **Retitle or refile as part of rename.** A rename changes the stem only; metadata and
  the reference-type directory remain stable.

Evidence: research report
`research:202610/bob_ref_rename_command/bob_ref_rename_command.md`; plan
`plan:202610/bob_ref_rename.md` (identity invariants and scratch-vault experiment A);
epic `bob-cli-7x`, phases `bob-cli-7x.3`, `bob-cli-7x.4`, and `bob-cli-7x.7`
(`docs/ref.md` and `tests/cli/ref_library/rename.rs`).

**Cost.** File paths and inbound links change while identity metadata remains
stable, so clients must follow the report's new path without treating the new
filename as a new reference. Annotated references and directory moves remain
unsupported. Browser bookmarks and copied `obsidian://` or `highlights://` URIs
cannot be updated by the vault rename.

**Reopens when.** The reference or reading-task identity contract changes, or
annotated renames gain a safe method that preserves highlight IDs and follow-up
links.

Superseded in part: the claim that a rename keeps the reference `id`, PDF marker, and PDF bytes is replaced by [Reference Ids Follow File Stems](#reference-ids-follow-file-stems); the `^ref-…` block ID, title, `source_url`, and dates still stay.

## Reference Sources Are Preserved Write-Once {#reference-sources-are-preserved-write-once}

**Status:** Accepted

bob preserves render-input Markdown and its derived code catalog in a hidden, content-addressed .bob store; source bytes are write-once and reference notes carry a note-local source_markdown pointer.

**Applies to.** bob-cli reference creation, intake, overwrite, backfill, and the
Bob Refs clients.

**Claim.** Preserve the exact Markdown bytes consumed by pandoc in
`.bob/ref-sources/<ref_type>/<birth-stem>--<hash12>/source.md`, alongside the
render-time `code.json` catalog. The source file is write-once: matching content
reuses it, while a digest mismatch refuses replacement. Keep the source outside
`lib/` and exclude `.bob/` from bob's note walkers. A reference note's
`source_markdown` frontmatter field points to the store. Derive that pointer at
birth by matching reference type, stem, and PDF digest; overwrite and verified
attach set it explicitly. Preserve old stores as history when content changes.

**Why.** The research found that 449 of 538 reports had code, with 70 blocks
containing literal tabs and 47% containing lines longer than 80 columns. PDF text
extraction loses tabs, wraps lines, and drops glyphs, so keeping the original
render input preserves exact copy bytes. A content-addressed hidden store keeps
those bytes and their catalog together, survives overwrite history, and avoids
the Highlights sidecar namespace. `lib/<stem>.md` conflicts with Highlights
annotations; other files under `lib/` are indexed and walked. Embedded PDF files
add a coordinated PDF write path and may not survive Highlights saves. The
note-local pointer keeps source metadata out of the PDF marker and avoids
rewriting annotated PDFs during backfill; it is derived once from the PDF digest
at note birth.

**Cost.** Source Markdown, including comments and frontmatter, is synced in the
private vault. Stores accumulate as history, and readers must validate digests
and tolerate missing catalogs. The pointer depends on birth-time PDF identity
and remains note-local.

**Reopens when.** A real collision or recovery issue shows content-addressed
history is unsafe, or the vault's privacy/sync model changes enough that syncing
the preserved Markdown is no longer acceptable.

Evidence: `research:202610/ref_code_block_copy/ref_code_block_copy.md`; bob-cli
`01f7ec97` (walker exclusion), `c7ced497` (render-time catalog), `009060f9`
(write-once source store and note pointer), `a6d3ecbf` (overwrite lifecycle),
`36ae0ef0` (verified attachment); Bob Mac Capture `d8a828f` (catalog models),
`c7a5f37` (Copy card integration).

## References Are Ingested At Birth {#references-are-ingested-at-birth}

**Status:** Accepted

The creating host files each reference under the maintenance and scan locks, queues locally when unsafe, and leaves annotation sync to the Mac.

**Applies to.** bob-cli and the vault hosts.

**Claim.** The host that renders a reference files it under
`bob_sync.lock → scan.lock`, with a pre-sync and one scoped commit. If it cannot
ingest safely, the PDF stays in that host's `xlib/` for its local intake drain.
Annotation sync remains the Mac's full scan.

**Why.** The research measured a median 4.6-minute delay, an 11.6-hour maximum,
and a 24% rate of commits that contained a new library PDF without its note.
Option G closes that split-commit window and makes a reference available from
the creating host without waiting for the Mac. It rejects A's tighter Mac cron
and B's SSH nudge because neither works while the Mac sleeps; C's filesystem
watchers are unreliable or Linux-only; D's full scan on each host breaks the
single annotation writer and widens the partial-commit window; E's tracked
`xlib/` duplicates binary Git churn and makes athena a single point of failure;
F's athena outbox is sound but more complex than needed unless real
cross-host collisions appear.

**Cost.** Agents' creates commit to the vault, and parent-note merges rely on
Git.

**Reopens when.** `_conflicts/sync_conflicts.md` shows same-stem collisions;
revisit the single-publisher design then.

Evidence: `research:202610/ref_create_auto_ingest_across_tailnet/ref_create_auto_ingest_across_tailnet.md`;
`plan:202610/ref_ingest_at_birth.md`; bob-cli `85eac25` (writing-scan lock),
`c4ac06f` (create ingest), `fa7745f` (intake-only drain), `5848c39` (producer
ingest), and `4703619` (intake health).

## Relation Card Tab Accepts Ctrl-D Hides {#relation-card-tab-accepts-ctrl-d-hides}

**Status:** Accepted

Ctrl+N/P navigate the relation card without touching the query, Tab accepts or completes the top match, selection is by key, and Ctrl+D hides what Return would insert.

**Applies to.** The Bob Mac Capture relation card and the Obsidian
relation-label stage.

**Claim.** Card state is `query`, `selectedKey` (a label key, never an array
index), and the catalog fetched once on open. Navigation changes only
`selectedKey` and the sentence pill: it never edits the query, spawns a
process, or clears freshness. Typing clears the selection and refreshes only
the typed-row validation probe; the list ranks locally from the catalog. Tab
accepts the selected row, or completes the top match when nothing is
selected. One rule ties the keys together: Ctrl+D hides what Return would
insert (a ghost row with undo on a selection, the one-off toggle otherwise).
Ctrl+H shows or hides the Hidden section; selection is by key so a refresh
keeps the key when it survives and clears it when it disappears.

**Why.** Writing the chosen row back into the field and refetching collapsed
the list to one typed row, so Tab computed `(0+1) mod 1 = 0` forever and fast
Tabs walked a stale list; the index also outlived its list, started at 0
(skipping the most-used label), and was never drawn. Index-based selection
cannot survive a reorder; key-based selection can. Rejected alternatives:

- **Tab cycles suggestions** — the reported bug: refetch-per-accept makes
  every Tab a no-op on a one-row list.
- **Index-based selection** — a reorder silently moves the highlight to a
  different row.
- **Fetch per keystroke for the list** — navigation must be local and instant;
  only the typed-row probe may call bob.
- **Ctrl+Shift+H for the Hidden section** — the accepted `hidden_key`
  branch is Ctrl+H, mirroring `bob relations -H`; Ctrl+H claims
  backward-delete only inside this one-line card.

Evidence: `plan:202610/relation_label_vocabulary.md` RV5 with
`hidden_key = ctrl_h`; `research:202610/relation_card_label_vocabulary`;
`docs/task-relations.md` §16.

**Cost.** Ctrl+H loses its Emacs backward-delete meaning inside the one-line
card field (Backspace and fn-Delete still delete). Footers must teach the
keys because Tab no longer cycles.

**Reopens when.** The Hidden section needs a different chord, navigation must
refetch, or selection must survive a key disappearing.

## Relation Label Hide Is Suggestions-Only {#relation-label-hide-is-suggestions-only}

**Status:** Accepted

Hiding a relation label removes it from suggestions only; LINKS text, mirrors, chips, counts, and typed use stay unchanged, and using it never unhides it.

**Applies to.** bob-cli `bob relations hide` / `unhide`, capture-complete
`relation_label` rows, the Mac relation card, and the Obsidian relation-label
stage.

**Claim.** Hiding a relation label removes it from **suggestions** only: card
rows, the Obsidian stage, `relations list` defaults, and shell completion.
LINKS text, LINKED FROM mirrors, chips, counts, and typed use are unchanged.
Typing a hidden label's exact name still works and is flagged `hidden`; using
it never unhides it. A one-off `||` label hides only after the capture's notes
commit succeeds, and hiding a visible existing label warns with the link count
instead of blocking. This is the twin of
[Hiding A Theme Removes It From Recent Only](#theme-hide-is-recent-only).

**Why.** Deleting a hidden label from the catalog would rewrite history and
lose its count. Auto-unhiding on use would fight the hide gesture the next
time the label is typed. Blocking typed use of a hidden label would make old
notes un-linkable. Auto-hiding anything (for example low-count labels) would
create silent state Bryan never asked for. Rejected alternatives:

- **Delete from the catalog** — Stats-equivalent counts and old LINKS lines
  would lose the name.
- **Unhide on next use** — typing a hidden label once would bounce it back
  into every suggestion list.
- **Block inserting hidden labels** — existing notes carrying the label could
  no longer be linked with it.
- **Auto-hide** — any silent hide breaks the no-silent-state rule; every hide
  is an explicit Ctrl+D, `bob relations hide`, or `||`.

Evidence: `plan:202610/relation_label_vocabulary.md` RV4;
`research:202610/relation_card_label_vocabulary`;
`docs/task-relations.md` §16; commits `57d77612`, `6def3ac8`, `895b9ba7`.

**Cost.** Hidden labels still occupy the catalog and still wear counts. Clients
must filter suggestions after ranking, not drop the catalog row, and must
render bob's warning message instead of computing the count.

**Reopens when.** Hide should also suppress counts or mirrors, typed use of a
hidden label should refuse, or using a hidden label should be an unhide
gesture.

## Relation Label Prefs Live In A Per-Host Journal {#relation-label-prefs-live-in-per-host-journal}

**Status:** Accepted

Relation label hide, unhide, and rename events live in vault-synced .bob/relations/<host>.jsonl; fold is last-writer-wins and bob is the only writer.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, Bob Mac Capture, and Obsidian plugins that hide,
unhide, or rename relation labels.

**Claim.** Preferences live in `.bob/relations/<host>.jsonl`, one
append-only file per host inside the vault so Git syncs them. `host` is the
same label vault-sync uses in commit subjects. Events are `v: 1`
`relation_label.hide`, `relation_label.unhide`, and `relation_label.rename`
(`from`, `to`, plus display names), each with `v`, `ts`, `host`, and `via`.
Fold is exactly the theme rule, implemented once in the shared `pref_journal`
module: read every `*.jsonl` file, skip malformed lines with a bounded
warning, sort by `(ts instant, host, path, line)`, and let the last writer win
per key. A rename moves the source key's explicit state unless the target
already has state; events after a rename on the old key apply to the old key.
bob is the only writer; other clients call bob. This is the twin of
[Theme Preferences Live In A Per-Host Journal](#theme-prefs-live-in-per-host-journal).

**Why.** Frontmatter on daily notes would mix derived history with
preferences. A machine-local file would not sync hides across apollo and the
Mac. A single shared JSON file would lose concurrent host appends; the
append-only per-host journal plus union merge keeps both hosts' writes.
Rejected alternatives:

- **Daily-note frontmatter** — every hide would dirty today's ledger.
- **Machine-local store** — a hide on apollo would not reach the Mac.
- **One shared JSON object** — two hosts writing at once would clobber.

Evidence: `plan:202610/relation_label_vocabulary.md` RV3;
`research:202610/relation_card_label_vocabulary`;
`docs/task-relations.md` §16; commit `57d77612`.

**Cost.** Fold must skip malformed lines. Rename is a logged event plus a
note rewrite, not a journal-only alias. Writers serialize through bob under
`bob_sync.lock`.

**Reopens when.** Concurrent host folds mis-order clocks often enough to need
a vector clock, or preferences must live outside the vault.

## Relation Label Rename Rewrites History {#relation-label-rename-rewrites-history}

**Status:** Accepted

bob relations rename rewrites matching label spans everywhere, including done/ and the previous daily note, in one previewed transaction and one revertable commit.

**Applies to.** bob-cli `bob relations rename`, the Mac card Ctrl+R rename
mode, and the Obsidian relation-label stage rename mode.

**Claim.** A rename runs one previewed transaction and makes one revertable
commit (`bob relations rename: OLD → NEW`). It rewrites only matching label
spans on accepted LINKS and LINKED FROM lines across the whole catalog scope,
including `done/` and the previous daily note — the recorded LR7 exception:
label spans only, never reopening tasks, minting IDs, pruning edges, or
reordering entries. Planning refuses (`malformed_links_line`, `stale_note`)
rather than under-covering. Preview lists every file and changed line, link
and mirror counts including `done/`, hidden-state and inverse changes, and
NEW's `replacement` forms. Undo is `git revert` of the one commit.

**Why.** Renaming without touching `done/` would leave history disagreeing
with the catalog and resurface OLD in suggestions via `renamed_reappeared`
forever. Rewriting without a single commit would make the rename
un-revertable. Covering malformed lines silently would corrupt notes the
rescan cannot verify. The shared `vault_rewrite` transaction (extracted from
`bob themes rename`) gives lock, pre-sync, snapshot, stale check, atomic
write with rollback, verify, one commit, and post-sync in one place. Rejected
alternatives:

- **Exclude done/ and old dailies** — history keeps the old spelling and the
  catalog never converges.
- **Rewrite without a commit** — no atomic undo; `git revert` stops working.
- **Skip malformed lines silently** — unverifiable partial coverage; refuse
  instead.
- **Journal-only alias** — OLD text stays in notes, so every scan keeps
  counting it.

Evidence: `plan:202610/relation_label_vocabulary.md` RV8;
`research:202610/relation_card_label_vocabulary`;
`docs/task-relations.md` §16; commits `fd9380cb`, `4c46dadd`.

**Cost.** Malformed or concurrently changed targets refuse instead of
renaming. Offline runs refuse dirty paths. Clients must render the preview
and merge arming from bob's JSON, never their own grammar.

**Reopens when.** A rename must touch more than label spans, must cover
unreadable notes, or `done/` must become fully read-only again.

## Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review {#review-walk-is-tiered}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Recurring Occurrences Walk When Due](#recurring-occurrences-walk-when-due)

The ]s walk visits one shared queue in explicit tiers PRE → NEW → PROJECTS → PENDING → NEXT → TICKLER → REFERENCES → ROTTEN → POST; #gtd #pre/#post checklist rows resolve only by completion; Pending and Next come due daily under pending_interval / next_interval (default 1, false walks that lane off); tiers never feed buckets or chips; upkeep outside the lanes counts the budget; stamps stay and the seed never re-runs.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault, dash.

**Claim.** The morning walk is a structural tier order in the shared
evaluator (Rust plus JavaScript, kept in sync under the walk vectors):
PRE → NEW → PROJECTS → PENDING → NEXT → TICKLER → REFERENCES → ROTTEN →
POST, with per-tier comparators in `docs/freshness.md` §4. Checklist
membership is exact whole-token tags, case-insensitive: `#gtd` plus
`#pre` is PRE, `#gtd` plus `#post` without `#pre` is POST. Checklist
scope admits open status symbols ` `, `*`, `/`, and `?`; recurring,
canonical daily-note, and Today-linked rows are admitted; hidden,
dependency-blocked, future-scheduled, and template/conflict rows are
not. Checklist rows resolve only by completion through Tasks, never by
a stamp. PRE is a commitment tier; POST is the closing tier after
ROTTEN that `]S` reaches. Pending (`[/]`) and Next (`[*]`) tasks come due
for a daily review set by `pending_interval` / `next_interval` (integer
1–365 or `false`; absent or null means the default 1). A walked lane's
interval overrides the whole Ready chain for that task (`[refresh::]`,
note `task_refresh`, `freshness.interval`); `false` walks that lane off
and its tasks fall back to the Ready chain. Tiers are due-only: a task
stamped today drops out of the walk, and recurring, daily-note, hidden,
dependency-blocked, future-scheduled, and Today-linked tasks are in no
tier except as PRE/POST checklist rows. The walk stays out of buckets
and chips: `state()`, `bucket()`, NEW and READY gating, the
`B = NEW ∪ TICKLER ∪ ROTTEN ∪ READY` partition, and the dash chips are
unchanged, and lane rows carry null `state`/`bucket`. The upkeep budget
counts today's stamps on tasks outside the lanes (`upkeep_today`), and
every `✓` meter shows that number. No stamps are stripped or flattened
and `bob freshness seed` never re-runs: the seeded `[fresh::]` dates
come due by 2026-10-08 and are truthful after that.

Rejected alternatives:

- **One interval-sorted queue.** A single `[refresh:: 1]` Ready task
  would outrank a Next task; the tier order is structural, not emergent.
- **A `scheduled` interval key.** A 1-day leash on every past-`scheduled`
  task would bring 59+ tasks back each morning. "Reviewed on the day it
  is due" is the TICKLER tier instead. Reopen as an opt-in Ready-only
  key if Bryan wants the daily nag.
- **Lanes always in the walk.** The `false` off-switch returns to
  Ready-only tiers (NEW → TICKLER → ROTTEN) with no code change.
- **A nav-only walk.** Both evaluators implement the contract; nav
  renders what the shared queue says.
- **Lanes in `bucket = rotten`.** Buckets and chips keep their partition;
  tiers are a separate walk dimension.
- **Stripping or flattening stamps.** That would turn about 150–200 tasks
  NEW at once; the census stays read-only.
- **An escalation sub-tier.** Deferred tickler tasks roll their P-level;
  no extra tier tracks them.
- **A Ready default of 1.** The Ready backlog keeps its 7-day cadence;
  only the lanes default to daily.
- **A second keymap or gtd-only walk.** PRE/POST join the one shared
  queue; `]s` is still the walk.
- **Membership by file path, block ID, inline field, or nested tag.**
  Exact `#gtd` plus `#pre`/`#post` tokens are the only members.
- **Lifting the recurring exclusion for every task.** Only tagged
  checklist rows admit recurrence, daily notes, Today, and `[?]`.
- **Dropping `repeat`.** Recurrence still writes the next occurrence;
  completion is the resolution.
- **POST before ROTTEN.** Reopen if `]S` is pressed at the boundary
  with zero ROTTEN done on most mornings.
- **Auto-completing Morning review.** Checking it is the closeout.

Evidence:
`research:202610/tiered_morning_review_walk/tiered_morning_review_walk.md`;
`plan:202610/tiered_morning_review_walk.md`;
`research:202610/gtd_pre_post_review_tiers` (artifact
`file:explicit:715e310d22ca404995bfa4a6`);
`plan:202610/gtd_pre_post_review_tiers.md`;
`docs/freshness.md` §§2/4/6/7/10–13 and schema 9 in bob-cli;
`api.freshness` namespace v4 in bob-ledger-tools;
tier notices, walk anchor, and lane-aware refresh row in
bob-navigation-hotkeys 1.50.0.

**Cost.** About 25 lane decisions a day at the caps (≤ 10 pending,
≤ 15 next); the rubber-stamp risk of a daily lane queue; two evaluators
kept in sync under the Q/L/R/S/B vectors.

**Reopens when.** The lane keep rate stays above 90% after lengthening
`next_interval`, or long-interval tasks starve past the weekly prune,
or PRE rows are skipped with `]s` on most mornings (then the habits
leave `#task`).

Amended in place 2026-10-04 at Bryan's request: the freshness trial was removed; nothing waits on it.

Amended in place 2026-10-04 at Bryan's request: PRE/POST checklist tiers.

Links [Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived](#task-lanes-are-sticky) (its "daily review with release"
cost) and [READY Is Freshness-Gated With NEW and ROTTEN Review](#ready-is-freshness-gated) (its partition, chips, and
gating claims stand; only the review ritual order is superseded in part).

Amended in place 2026-10-07 at Bryan's request: the RETURNED walk tier is renamed TICKLER (machine tier `tickler`, footer label TICKS); the Ready state stays `resurfaced`.

Superseded in part: the walk order PRE → NEW → PROJECTS → PENDING → NEXT → TICKLER → REFERENCES → ROTTEN → POST; "recurring, daily-note, hidden, dependency-blocked, future-scheduled, and Today-linked tasks are in no tier except as PRE/POST checklist rows"; the REFERENCES tier; occupancy and frontmatter-`scheduled` PROJECTS gating; and the rejected alternative "Lifting the recurring exclusion for every task", now narrowed so recurring rows still never enter NEW or ROTTEN — see [Recurring Occurrences Walk When Due](#recurring-occurrences-walk-when-due).

## Rotten Keeps Are Logged {#rotten-keeps-are-logged}

**Status:** Accepted

Every counted keep — Alt+F/Ctrl+Alt+F on an exact due Ready ROTTEN or scheduled TICKLER row, or the decay card's Keep — asks an optional reason and writes one dated 🥀 ROTTEN LOG entry with the stamp; the entry count is display-only history, never a field or a decay input.

**Applies to.** bob-plugins (bob-navigation-hotkeys, bob-ledger-tools), bob-cli
(managed-log registry, agenda JSON, note snapshots, docs), Bob Mac Capture (agenda
chip), and the vault.

**Claim.** A counted keep is an exact, due, Ready rotten/tickler target that the
single keep helper would increment: an exact pre-write queue row in the Ready lane
with tier rotten or scheduled tickler, not returned by an unblock, not already
