stamped today, and confirmed by a dry run of the keep helper. Every counted keep —
a single Alt+F/Ctrl+Alt+F press below the decay limit, the decay card's Keep,
counted `N<Alt+F>` targets, and Task Link counted targets — first asks "Why keep
it as written?" and then writes exactly one dated entry under a `🥀 **ROTTEN LOG**`
direct child in the same transaction as the stamp, with one undo. The reason is
optional: a blank answer logs `🤷 no reason given`. Esc writes nothing: no stamp,
no entry, no advance. The entry reads `*YYYY-MM-DD* — <reason> · kept N×` with
the local review date, newest first directly under the marker; N is the
[[keep-streak]] after that keep, 1–999. The log is audit and display only: its
count ("N keeps logged") never resets, is never stored as a field, and nothing
reads it to change decay, buckets, tiers, lanes, Today, schedule, priority, or
[Task Freshness](../reference/glossary.md#task-freshness). NEW, early/FRESH, Pending, Next, PROJECTS, recurring,
checklist, closed, and unblock-tickler keeps never prompt and never write it;
Pending summaries stay in the [Work Log](../reference/glossary.md#work-log) and deferrals in the
[Schedule Log](../reference/glossary.md#schedule-log). `bob capture`, Rust, hooks, randomize, and seed never write it.
There is no backfill: keeps before rollout leave no entries.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Nonblank-only entries.** A blank reason logs `🤷 no reason given`; the entry is
  never optional.
- **Logging every Alt+F.** Only counted keeps log; uncounted stamps stay silent.
- **ROTTEN tier only.** Scheduled ticklers log; unblock ticklers do not.
- **A lifetime field or numeral by the mark.** The entry count is display-only and
  never stored on the task line.
- **Schedule- or Work-Log storage.** Keeps get their own `🥀 **ROTTEN LOG**` child.
- **The journal as the store.** The log lives with the task and travels with it.
- **A second-keep gate.** Every counted keep prompts, from the first.

Evidence:
`research:202610/rotten_log_keep_history/rotten_log_keep_history.md`;
`plan:202610/rotten_log.md`;
`docs/freshness.md` §2a and `docs/task-dependencies.md` §2.4 in bob-cli.

**Cost.** One more kind in the closed registry across Rust and every plugin parser;
a two-key keep (Alt+F, then Enter); log growth of about four lines a month on a
weekly-kept reading task; two numbers to keep apart (resetting streak vs.
never-reset logged count); editable, not tamper-proof Markdown.

**Reopens when.** A month of entries is more than 80% `🤷`, or counted keeps exceed
about five per morning (consider a from-the-second-keep gate), or the log goes
unread.

Supersedes in part [Rotten Keeps Decay Through The Priority Ladder](#rotten-keeps-use-priority-decay) for the
rejection of a new REVIEW LOG structure and "Keep anyway leaves only the line
increment" only; counting, explicit consent, the priority ladder, and the other
card outcomes stand.

## Rotten Keeps Decay Through The Priority Ladder {#rotten-keeps-use-priority-decay}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Decay Decisions Are Available Immediately](#decay-decisions-are-available-immediately), [Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers), [Rotten Keeps Are Logged](#rotten-keeps-are-logged)

Repeated due-Ready keeps earn an explicit approved decision that enters the existing priority ladder; nothing decays silently and freshness itself still never changes priority or schedule.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** The stored `[keeps:: N]` field is a streak of due-Ready bare keeps
(how many consecutive due reviews confirmed the task as written), not a
lifetime refresh counter; absence means 0 and writers omit zero. Only an
exact, due, Ready rotten/tickler target increments, once per review, through
the single JavaScript helper `api.freshness.keepLine`; every other human stamp
clears the streak, and automation, hooks, randomize, and seed neither
increment nor reset. At the configured limit (default 3) the next due
Alt+F/Alt+Shift+F press opens an explicit consent card — Not now, Less often,
Reword, Drop, Keep — and writes nothing until Bryan chooses; Enter can defer
but never cancels from that card. Approved schedule-changing decisions reuse
the existing priority roll/decay ladder and log writers with `· kept N×`
reason tails; Keep anyway just counts again. Freshness itself still never
changes a lane, Today, schedule, or priority. Repeated keeps earn a question
about urgency, never an automatic change.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Lifetime `refresh_count` or a second alias counter.** One streak field;
  no backfill: seeded, captured, and old `fresh` stamps are not evidence
  of keeps.
- **Silent auto-decay at the limit.** The card asks; nothing changes
  without an explicit choice.
- **Counting non-Ready lanes or NEW tasks.** Only due Ready
  rotten/tickler targets count; other targets stamp and preserve.
- **Timer-fired cards.** A card still requires an explicit gesture after
  the 2026-10-19 activation date, never a background write.
- **A new REVIEW LOG structure.** Decisions reuse the existing Schedule,
  Cancel, and Work logs; Keep anyway leaves only the line increment.

Evidence:
`research:202610/rotten_keep_streak_and_approved_decay/rotten_keep_streak_and_approved_decay.md`;
`plan:202610/rotten_keep_streak.md`;
`docs/freshness.md` §§2a/7/10a/11 and `docs/projects.md` ("Approved-decay
decision planner") in bob-cli; `api.freshness.keepLine` (namespace v5) plus
the FreshnessDecayCardModal in bob-ledger-tools 1.24.0 /
bob-navigation-hotkeys 1.69.0; shared vectors
`tests/fixtures/freshness_keeps/vectors.json`.

**Cost.** Two implementations (Rust read/clear/report plus JavaScript
count/display/decide) stay in sync under the shared vectors; the scalar is
not an exact global event counter (git sync may lose an increment, caches
under-count, hand edits stay unobserved). Calibration is a lightweight
human tally, never telemetry or automatic tuning.

**Reopens when.** The post-activation calibration tally shows the limit
misfires (mostly Keep suggests 4, mostly Drop suggests 2), or the recorded
trial extends the 2026-10-19 boundary.

Superseded in part: 2026-10-19 activation boundary and the
trial-extension reopening condition only — see
[Decay Decisions Are Available Immediately](#decay-decisions-are-available-immediately). Counting,
explicit consent, priority/log writers, and exclusion rules stand.

Amended in place 2026-10-07 at Bryan's request: the RETURNED walk tier is renamed TICKLER (machine tier `tickler`, footer label TICKS); the Ready state stays `resurfaced`.

Superseded in part: a keep on an unblock tickler leaves the streak
unchanged — see [Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers).

Superseded in part: the rejection of a new REVIEW LOG structure and

consent, the priority ladder, and the other card outcomes stand.

## Similar Tasks Are A Settled Heads-Up {#similar-tasks-are-a-settled-heads-up}

**Status:** Accepted

Capture shows a "Similar tasks" band only after typing settles and only when a match clears bob's calibrated bars; every row action is an explicit draft edit and Return never changes.

# Similar Tasks Are A Settled Heads-Up

*Accepted · project*

aka similar tasks band, duplicate heads-up

**Applies to.** Bob Mac Capture, bob-cli.

**Claim.** When a capture draft will create new tasks, the preview shows a
"Similar tasks" band at the foot of the new task's own preview card. It is a
heads-up, never a gate:

- A row carries a **Same title** or **Possible duplicate** mark only when the
  evidence supports it. No percentages, and no score is ever shown as a
  probability.
- **Zero pixels unless a match clears the bar.** No header, no placeholder,
  never a "No duplicates" line.
- **Settle-gated.** bob is asked after about 350 ms without edits, on its own
  cancellable lane. Rows on screen hold while the user types and swap only if
  the settled result changed.
- **Scope.** Every open task in routable notes, plus tasks closed in the last
  30 days at the duplicate bar only (at most 1 row).
- **Gate.** Only items that create a task: `task`, `pomodoro_task`, and the
  `^prj` title of `project_note` / `pomodoro_project_note`. Require at least 2
  meaningful terms, with a stricter bar under 3 terms except for an exact title
  match. `@@template:` drafts are skipped.
- **Cap.** 2 rows for a single-item draft plus a "+N" capsule, 1 row per item
  in bulk drafts, at most 5 per draft.
- **Actions are explicit draft edits only.** The strip's keys are the capture
  sigils (`~` relate, `+` add as note, `&` needs it, `*` blocks it, `/` open,
  `⌫` discard mine). Return is never intercepted or re-confirmed, nothing is
  auto-linked, and `@` and `!` are not v1 actions. The ↩ default is split:
  ⌫ Discard mine for Same title, + Add as note for Possible duplicate.
- **Numbers.** Zero extra spawns per keystroke. Preview p95 is unchanged with
  the feature on versus off. The related lane's p95 on the Mac is at most
  50 ms.
- **Settings toggle** ("Show similar tasks while capturing", on by default).
  Thresholds live in bob, not in Settings.
- **Calibrated bars** (`bob capture-related`, schema_version 1):
  `POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE` 0.70, `SIMILAR` 0.48, `CLOSED_DUPLICATE` 0.70,
  `HOLD_MARGIN` 0.10, `SHORT_QUERY_BOOST` 0.10, `MIN_TERMS` 2 — with
  closed-class function-word stopwords, single-digit numbers kept as terms,
  and a number guard (titles whose number sets differ are never duplicates).
  Measured on the 496-query leave-one-out census: possible_duplicate precision
  6/6, similar usefulness 39/54 (72.2%), firing 55/496 (11.1%, about 1 capture
  in 9). Mac release p95 is 43.494 ms against the 50 ms gate.
- **bob owns meaning; the app owns timing and pixels.** Eligibility, tokens,
  weights, bands, hysteresis, exclusions, action availability, defaults,
  splice anchors, and replacement strings come from `bob capture-related`.
  The app schedules the call, holds and fits rows, and applies the edits bob
  describes.

**Why.** The research showed wording reliably finds the same work captured
twice but does not find workflow relations: on 95 real dependency pairs the
true prerequisite ranked top-5 only about 20% of the time — so the UI promises
a duplicate heads-up, not relations. The Mac turned out fast (4.7 ms spawn,
21 ms open-task scan), so one per-settle subprocess call meets the 50 ms gate
with no in-app index. TF-IDF over Bob-aware tokens beat the picker's
all-terms matcher (3% fire rate, missed paraphrases) and plain Dice (missed
stemmed duplicates). Calibrated from 80 reviewed leave-one-out pairs labeled
under Bryan's delegation (10 D / 47 U / 23 N): scalar thresholds alone capped
possible_duplicate precision at 60% until the number guard and stopword fixes
reached 6/6. These are agent judgments, not Bryan-authored labels, and the
figures are in-sample, not held-out.

Rejected alternatives:

- **A "related tasks" list.** Matching cannot deliver workflow relations, so
  the band must not promise them.
- **An in-app index for v1.** Measured latency leaves headroom; the index
  stays a measured escalation path if the gate ever breaks.
- **Embeddings, Dice, or the picker's all-terms matcher.** Unjustified cost,
  missed stemmed duplicates, or a 3% fire rate respectively.
- **↩ adds as note for both (`duplicate_default = note_both`).** An exact
  recapture is almost always a forgotten task; a lexical near-match may not
  be.
- **Shipping the research's starting bars (`calibration = starting_bars`).**
  The bars come from labels, and the starting 0.55 similar bar fired at only
  6.7% with 60% duplicate precision.
- **A closed bar above 0.82.** It would read 2/2 but rests on one pair;
  re-check when more closed pairs accumulate.
- **An abbreviation table** (appt vs appointment). Vocabulary-specific; add
  only if future labels show recurring misses.

**Cost.** Every capture feature lands twice, bob-cli first, and the Mac half
is gated by macOS CI. The JSON contract grows additively at schema_version 1
with old-bob fallback. Thresholds retune in bob, never in Settings. The band
folds to one line before it can cause scrolling, and held rows render only to
keep an already-visible row steady.

**Reopens when.** The 50 ms gate breaks on measured Mac hardware (escalate to
the in-app index); closed-pair evidence accumulates enough to revisit the
closed bar; abbreviation misses recur in labels; or firing drifts far from
about 1 capture in 9 on real captures rather than the title-census proxy.

Evidence: `research:202610/capture_similar_tasks_band/capture_similar_tasks_band.md`;
`plan:202610/capture_similar_tasks_band.md`; epic `bob-cli-ab` phases
`bob-cli-ab.1`–`bob-cli-ab.7`; bob-cli `787d62cb` (engine), `062fc3da`
(contract), `453dc4a7` (calibration); calibration report and Mac timing in the
research sidecar (`202610/capture_similar_tasks_band/calibration.md`,
`calibration_mac_timing_final.json`).

[Bob Mac Capture Is A Thin Client Of bob](#mac-capture-is-a-thin-client)

[Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked](#unblocked-tasks-are-offered)

[Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites](#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps)

[An Empty Capture Draft Shows Today's Ledger Agenda](#idle-capture-shows-ledger-agenda)

## Sub-projects Inherit Project Blocking {#subprojects-inherit-project-blocking}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked](#unblocked-tasks-are-offered)

A blocked project passes its dependency or schedule reason through its project descendants, with reconcile as the authority and the ^prj tag as the proxy for other engines.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** A project note has at most one parent, stored as a scalar frontmatter
`parent:` wikilink. The exact vault-relative path wins; otherwise only a unique,
case-insensitive basename resolves. List-form, ambiguous, unresolved, self, terminal,
and non-project parents do not create inheritance. Every active project inherits each
ancestor's own `^prj` Blocked reason, nearest ancestor first. An inherited `^prj` is
Blocked `[?]` and tagged `#prj_is_blocked`; every open resident is Blocked and tagged
when its project is blocked by its own or an inherited reason. A project's own `^prj`
reason does not tag that same `^prj` line. Reconcile derives and reverses the cascade;
the tag is the stored proxy read by engines that do not walk the tree.

The Task Card applies and reverses the cascade in the same write for Depends on changes
and, under `schedule_cascade = yes`, Schedule changes to `^prj`. Other writers respect
the tag and leave descendant recovery to the next reconcile; `close_recovers_subprojects
= no`. When closing a child project's `^prj` makes its parent project empty, the parent
`^prj` is pulled in as Next (`docs/task-dependencies.md` §12.10 trigger (c)). A project's
prerequisite may not target a task in its own descendant.

**Why.** A blocked project's work must not reappear as Ready merely because it lives in a
child note. Reconcile already knows the project tree and all project reasons. Storing
the inherited fact on the child's `^prj` lets close paths and plugin link guards enforce
the same rule without copying dependency edges or walking the tree on every gesture.
Trigger (c) keeps a parent project moving when its last open child project closes.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Residence-only blocking.** A child's Ready lane would surface work that remains
  blocked by an ancestor.
- **Copying ancestor prerequisites or dates into descendants.** Duplicate edges and
  schedule fields create new writers and drift; the tag records the inherited fact.
- **Immediate descendant recovery on close or status cycling.** That expands each close
  into a tree write; reconcile repairs the tags on its next pass.
- **Stem matching ambiguous parents.** It can select the wrong note; only a unique
  basename may resolve when the exact path is absent.

Evidence: `plan:202610/subproject_cascade.md`; `docs/task-dependencies.md` §§12.10–13;
epic `bob-cli-78` and its contract, reconcile, close, and cycler phases; task-status-cycler
1.37.0 and block-id-prompt 1.30.0.

**Cost.** Non-Task-Card writers can leave descendants tagged until reconcile runs. The
project tree and tag proxy must stay consistent across Rust and plugin readers. A parent
`^prj` with a descendant target is refused to avoid a dependency cycle.

**Reopens when.** Projects need multiple parents, descendant recovery must happen
immediately outside the Task Card, or the parent relationship stops being a scalar
frontmatter wikilink.

Supersedes in part [Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line): blocking by residence
alone is retired; a project's own prerequisites and date still originate on its `^prj`.

Superseded in part: the parent project's trigger (c) pull-in is now offered and linked
only when picked. See [Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked](#unblocked-tasks-are-offered).

## Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line {#task-deps-are-depends-on-links}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites](#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps)

A task's prerequisites live as plain task dependency links on one managed Depends-On first-child line; that line is the source of truth and the [dependsOn::] / [id::] fields are derived from it.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** A task's prerequisites live as plain, never-transcluded [Task Link](../reference/glossary.md#task-link)s
on one managed `⛓️ **DEPENDS ON:**` first-child line. That line is the source of
truth: `bob task-status-hooks` derives the task's `[dependsOn::]` field and each
target's `[id::]` from it through R1–R10 reconciliation, and the task stays Blocked
`[?]` while any prerequisite is open. Linking the dependent under today's Pomodoros
raises its open prerequisites to Next; closing the dependent never closes its
targets. `docs/task-dependencies.md` owns the grammar, identity, link form,
reconciliation, and chip rules.

**Why.** Dependencies used to be inferred from any sole transcluded child, so the
Ctrl+Shift+P picker only saw the current note (44 of 45 edges were same-note),
`#^ref` reading embeds promoted tasks they merely quoted, closing an embedded
ledger link recursively closed its prerequisites, Ctrl+D on `dependsOn` orphaned
the embeds, and picker writes took several undo steps. One managed line with
plain links removes the inference: the picker fuzzy-searches every open task in
the vault, each write commits in one transaction, and live chips render each
link's status. Rejected alternatives:

- **Links only.** No derived field, so Tasks queries and Blocked derivation lose
  their whole-vault index.
- **Fields only with a virtual line.** Nothing readable or hand-editable in the
  note; hand edits have nowhere to land.
- **A field-authoritative generated line.** Writers would have to update the field
  and regenerate the line in lockstep; the line could never be the edit surface.
- **One bullet per dependency.** Unbounded children bloat the task block and
  collide with logs and notes.
- **Links on the task line.** No room for several prerequisites; the task line is
  already crowded with fields.
- **The Tasks modal as the editor.** It cannot be made a real editing surface, so
  its dependency edits to a task that has a line are dropped with a warning.
- **`!` as the gesture.** The transclusion toggle stays a pure toggle; dependency
  edits go through Ctrl+Shift+P → Depends on, so the gesture never rewrites the
  parent task line.
- **Stored aliases and strikes.** They break the canonical writer form and the
  chip model; reader tolerance plus canonicalisation covers hand variants.

**Cost.** Four parsers kept in sync by shared vectors (Rust, nav, ledger-tools,
cycler/block-id-prompt recognisers); the projection exists at all; deleting the
whole line outside Obsidian is re-adopted rather than honoured; Tasks-modal
dependency edits to a task that has a line are dropped; `#^ref` embeds no longer
promote.

**Reopens when.** R1/R2 warnings appear on most hooks runs for two weeks; the
Tasks modal becomes a real editing surface; Tasks' `is blocked` stops being
load-bearing.

Evidence: `research:202610/task_dep_link_depends_on_line/task_dep_link_depends_on_line.md`;
epic `bob-cli-3n` (`plan:202610/task_dep_links.md`); `docs/task-dependencies.md`
(`f4b0d12`); hooks parser and edges (`2d4d508`); R1–R10 reconciliation (`043d9c5`);
bob-plugins `1831db4` (chips), `e7baeb5` (compat), `5194bc8` (nav-model),
`08d1560` (nav-stage), `82aec34` (nav-gestures), `46ddd1e` (migration script);
vault migration `66c6d47c`; fix epic `bob-cli-3n.12`
(`plan:202610/task_dep_links_fixes.md`): bob-cli `8d54b0e` (hooks-correctness),
`b61727a` (api v1 line refusal), `a069239` (DP24–DP29), `79e39af`
(hooks-docs-cleanup); bob-plugins `3ffa187` (nav-writer-fix), `330fc58`
(chips-compat-fix), `f78ffad` (nav-mirror-gestures), `40e2e3a`
(nav-stage-polish).

Linking a dependency-blocked dependent from capture drops its open
prerequisites instead of raising them
([Capture Links A Dependency-Blocked Task By Dropping Its Prerequisites](#capture-link-drops-blocking-deps)).

## Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived {#task-lanes-are-sticky}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line)

Linking raises Ready to Next and an =x close sets In Progress (PENDING); no unlink, hooks run, or capture drop lowers them; only Alt+N release returns a task to Ready; Blocked stays derived.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, Bob Mac Capture, vault.

**Claim.** Lanes are sticky:

1. Adding a Task Link under today's open Pomodoros raises Ready `[ ]` or
   Blocked `[?]` to Next `[*]`; Next and Pending are unchanged.
2. An `=x` in-progress outcome sets `[/]` (unchanged).
3. Removing a link **never** changes the lane: the hooks, Ctrl+Shift+Enter,
   `@route+id!`, `=x~K`, `=~K`, and hand deletion.
4. Only **release** (Alt+N, or the Ctrl+Shift+P lane row) lowers Next or
   Pending to Ready. Releasing also removes the task's live links from today's
   open Pomodoros; releasing a Pending task offers the optional Work Log
   prompt.
5. Alt+N on a Ready task **commits** it to Next without linking it.
6. Blocked stays derived, overrides every lane, and recovers to the existing
   derived rank (Ready unless linked today or reached by recent activity).
7. **Carve-out (R9):** tasks that live in canonical daily notes (such as
   `^gtd`) keep today's derived clearing of `[*]`, including the
   recent-activity `KeptNext` grace.
8. **R12:** the `[/]` symbol, its "In Progress" name and IN_PROGRESS type
   stay. Only dash and chip labels say PENDING. Picker group names
   (`in_progress`) stay.

**Why.** Sticky lanes protect dropped work by default, where `#now` did only
if tagged before dropping. The one bulk `#now` tagging covered exactly the 73
`[/]` + `[*]` tasks and was stripped the same day. Bryan cancelled a separate
Submitted status ("WIP status should fill this role"). Swarm work needs a
quiet place to wait. Pending → Next → Ready is Kanban's pull order and matches
capture's `queued > in_progress > next`. Rejected alternatives:

- **Keep `#now` with a derived `[*]`.** It repeats Today.
- **A Submitted/Waiting status.** Bryan cancelled it; WIP fills the role.
- **No promotion on link.** That is the status-lock trap.
- **Age-based Next decay.** Not adopted, and never for Pending.
- **A hidden pre-block status.** No hidden previous-status field is stored.

Evidence:
`research:202609/retire_now_sticky_lanes_ledger_today/retire_now_sticky_lanes_ledger_today.md`;
epic `bob-cli-2y` (`plan:202609/retire_now_sticky_lanes.md`); phase
`bob-cli-2y.2` (hooks-sticky implementation and verification).

**Cost.** No automatic forgetting: about 2–3 tasks a day of lane growth at
September's rates, so caps, chips, lints, a daily review with release and a
weekly prune are required. `[/]` no longer means "worked recently". Lanes
don't survive Blocked. Dependency-promoted Next is sticky too. About 80 legacy
statuses need one-time triage.

**Reopens when.** Lanes must survive Blocked (then Blocked becomes an overlay).

Amended in place 2026-10-04 at Bryan's request: the freshness trial was removed; nothing waits on it.

Superseded in part: claim 1 no longer raises a Blocked task (its link is
consumed and its prerequisites rise), and "lanes don't survive Blocked"
is now project-wide — see [Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line).

## A Task Move Never Advances The Walk {#task-move-never-advances-the-walk}

**Status:** Accepted

Ctrl+Shift+M never advances the ]s walk, even from a landed row: it follows the moved task to its destination note and parks the walk, so the next ]s / [s resumes at the moved row's walk neighbour.

**Applies to.** bob-plugins (bob-navigation-hotkeys), bob-cli docs, and the Bob
vault review ritual.

**Claim.** Ctrl+Shift+M never advances the `]s` walk, even from a landed row:
it follows the moved task to its destination note and parks the walk, so the
next `]s` / `[s` resumes at the moved row's walk neighbour.

- The resume identifies rows by note path and line text, so the line shift a
  move causes never skips a row.
- The gesture lock still swallows Ctrl+Shift+M while another answer settles.
- Pomodoro bullet and entry moves were never part of the walk.
- Every other answer in [Answering A Walk Landing Advances The Walk](#answering-advances-the-walk) keeps
  advancing.

**Why.** Bryan keeps working on the task where it now lives; after moving it
he often adds context, dependencies, or a link in the destination note (his
answer in this plan's questions round).

Rejected alternatives:

- **Advancing instead of focusing (the epic `bob-cli-4l` rule, 2026-10-06).**
  It took Bryan away from the note where the follow-up work happens.
- **Staying in the source note without advancing.** The follow-up happens in
  the destination, and the seam is usually the next due row, which a bare
  `]s` from a due row steps past.
- **Restoring the pre-epic move unchanged.** Line-keyed anchors make the next
  `]s` skip the row below the moved task once the Tasks cache refreshes.
- **A per-gesture toggle or config switch.** That is one more setting for one
  key.

Evidence:
`plan:202610/ctrl_shift_m_never_advances_walk.md`;
bob-navigation-hotkeys 2.7.0 (this change);
`docs/freshness.md` §§6/13 in bob-cli.

**Cost.** Reaching the next review item after a move takes one `]s`. The
resume lives only until the next landing or stamp, so an Alt+F or Ctrl+Alt+F
elsewhere in between re-anchors the walk there.

**Reopens when.** Bryan finds himself pressing `]s` right after nearly every
move, or asks for the move to advance again.

Links [Answering A Walk Landing Advances The Walk](#answering-advances-the-walk) (the walk this move stays out
of) and [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](#review-walk-is-tiered) (the tier order the resume walks).

## Active Task Statuses Are Derived, Not Authored {#task-status-is-derived}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived](#task-lanes-are-sticky), [Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line](#task-deps-are-depends-on-links), [Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line)

Today's Pomodoro ledger drives Next and In Progress; open dependencies and future scheduled dates drive Blocked. bob task-status-hooks reconciles them, so writers change those inputs, never just the checkbox.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** Next `[*]`, In Progress `[/]`, and Blocked `[?]` are derived, not authored. A
task is Next while a Task Link to it, or a transcluded dependency path, sits under
today's open Pomodoros. It becomes `[/]` when an `=x` close records work on it, and in
area and project notes `[/]` resets once neither today's ledger nor the previous daily
links it. It is `[?]` while it has an open `dependsOn` target or a `scheduled` date
after today, which overrides the other two. `bob task-status-hooks` is the vault-wide
reconciler and runs unattended (every 15 minutes on the MacBook). Capture and the
plugins' keymaps may apply the same rules at once for feedback, but they change the
inputs — a Task Link, a dependency, a schedule — and the hooks have the final word.
`docs/task-status-hooks.md` owns the full rules and precedence table; see also
[Task Link](../reference/glossary.md#task-link).

**Why.** The authored status failed first: `[B]` Blocked was retired unused — no `#task`
line in the vault carried it — when Next replaced it (bob-plugins `890ed13`, `feat!`,
2026-07-08). Next was derived from open Pomodoros two days later (`bc829fa`), and
Blocked came back on 2026-07-16 as derived state (`fc39562`). Its plan,
`plan:202607/blocked_task_status.md`, calls Blocked "derived state, not a second
dependency model" and keeps the command "the vault-wide source of truth", because only a
whole-vault scan knows every remaining dependency: the `!` keymap sets `[?]` when it
adds a dependency but stays status-neutral when one is removed, for exactly that reason.
In Progress rollback followed on 2026-07-21 (`084bb62`) and future schedules on
2026-07-24 (`9bb625a`). Rejected alternatives: an authored Blocked status; letting each
command or keymap own the final status (an `=x` close deliberately leaves Blocked
recovery to the hooks); and keeping a hidden pre-block status to restore later.

**Cost.** A hand edit to a derived checkbox is silently undone on the next run, and
between runs the vault can look inconsistent. Every writer must keep the inputs
consistent: a hand unblock must also retire the future `scheduled` date, or the hooks
re-derive `[?]` (bob-plugins `786fc1d`). A recovered task returns to its derived rank,
not its pre-block status. Because statuses decay, "this matters this week" cannot live
in a checkbox — that is what [#now Is A User-Owned Weekly Bet, Never A Status](#now-tag-is-user-owned) is for.

**Reopens when.** A status is needed that no ledger, dependency, or schedule input can
express, or reconciliation moves off a periodic whole-vault scan (for example, behind a
transactional vault service).

Superseded in part: Next and In Progress are no longer derived — see
[Next And Pending Are Sticky Lanes; Only Blocked Is Derived](#task-lanes-are-sticky). The transcluded-dependency path and the `!`
removal rationale are retired by [Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line](#task-deps-are-depends-on-links);
the Blocked rule stands. The Blocked rule also inherits from the project —
see [Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line).

## Hiding A Theme Removes It From Recent Only {#theme-hide-is-recent-only}

**Status:** Accepted

Hiding a theme removes it from Recent suggestion rows only; today, Stats, colors, and typing the name stay unchanged, and using it never unhides it.

**Applies to.** bob-cli `bob themes`, capture-complete Recent rows, Obsidian
and Mac Pomodoro-name menus.

**Claim.** Hiding a theme removes it from **Recent** rows only. Today's ledger
rows, typing the name, history, Stats, and colors are unaffected. Using a hidden
name never unhides it. `bob themes list` omits hidden themes by default; `-H`
lists only them; `-a` lists every known theme and flags hidden ones.

**Why.** Deleting a theme from the catalog would rewrite history. Auto-unhiding
on use would fight the hide gesture the next morning. Muting colors on hide
would mix a suggestion preference with the hue rule. Rejected alternatives:

- **Delete from the catalog** — Stats and old daily notes would lose the name.
- **Unhide on next use** — a hidden name typed to start a Pomodoro would bounce
  back into Recent.
- **Hide also mutes color** — color would stop meaning identity.

Evidence: `plan:202610/pomodoro_themes.md` PT9; `docs/pomodoro-themes.md`.

**Cost.** Hidden themes still occupy Stats and still wear a hue. Menus must
filter Recent after ranking, not drop the catalog row.

**Reopens when.** Hide should also suppress Stats or color, or using a hidden
name should be an unhide gesture.

## Theme Hue Is Config Then Pin Then Exempt Then Unconfigured Then Area Then Hash {#theme-hue-is-config-pin-exempt-area-hash}

**Status:** Accepted

A theme's hue is configured themes color, then journal pin, then plan.exempt mute, then the unconfigured mute, then top-level area stem, then name hash; clients render the hue Bob reports.

**Applies to.** bob-cli catalog and JSON, Obsidian theme pills, Bob Mac Capture
swatches, terminal `bob themes` output.

**Claim.** Hue is resolved in order: a configured `themes:` color
(`hue_source: config`); else a journal pin (`hue_source: pin`); else a
normalized `plan.exempt` key is muted (`hue: null`, `hue_source: exempt`); else
a key outside the configured vocabulary is muted (`hue: null`,
`hue_source: unconfigured`); else a key equal to a top-level area note's stem
(parent `[[area]]`) wears that area's resolved hue (`hue_source: area`); else
`Hue::ALL[fnv1a32(key) % 8]` (`hue_source: hash`). Rust computes the hue.
Clients render the `hue` Bob reports and never hash or scan areas themselves.
Colors are stable, not unique; pins fix recurring collisions.

**Why.** Config beats pin because the user-owned file is the source of truth:
editing it must always take effect. A config color also beats the exempt mute,
so PLAN can wear blue and still not count toward `plan.max_themes`. Rejected
alternatives:

- **Pin beats config** — editing the config file would silently lose to an old
  journal pin.
- **Hex colors** — every surface already has a light/dark pair and an xterm-256
  code per palette slot; a hex color would render gray on the Mac and need
  derived variants everywhere.
- **A unique color per theme** — the palette is eight slots.

Evidence: `plan:202610/configured_pomodoro_themes.md` PT5 revised;
`docs/pomodoro-themes.md` PT5, PT12.

**Cost.** `bob themes color` refuses with `config_color` on a theme whose
config sets a color. Journal pins shadowed by a config color stay in the
journal untouched and apply again if that config color is removed. Every
client must wait for Bob's `hue` field.

**Reopens when.** The palette grows, area notes stop being the hue source for
matching stems, or a client needs a hue before Bob can answer.

Supersedes [Theme Hue Is Pin Then Exempt Then Area Then Hash](#theme-hue-is-pin-exempt-area-hash).

## Theme Hue Is Pin Then Exempt Then Area Then Hash {#theme-hue-is-pin-exempt-area-hash}

**Status:** Superseded by [Theme Hue Is Config Then Pin Then Exempt Then Unconfigured Then Area Then Hash](#theme-hue-is-config-pin-exempt-area-hash)

A theme's hue is journal pin, then plan.exempt mute, then top-level area stem, then name hash; clients render the hue Bob reports.

**Applies to.** bob-cli catalog and JSON, Obsidian theme pills, Bob Mac Capture
swatches, terminal `bob themes` output.

**Claim.** Hue is resolved in order: a journal pin (`hue_source: pin`); else a
normalized `plan.exempt` key is muted (`hue: null`, `hue_source: exempt`); else
a key equal to a top-level area note's stem (parent `[[area]]`) wears that
area's resolved hue (`hue_source: area`); else
`Hue::ALL[fnv1a32(key) % 8]` (`hue_source: hash`). Rust computes the hue.
Clients render the `hue` Bob reports and never hash or scan areas themselves.
Colors are stable, not unique; pins fix recurring collisions.

**Why.** Hash-only identity made JOB and BOB the same magenta, and GTD would
wear an area orange it does not mean. Unique colors cannot fit an unbounded
catalog in an eight-slot palette. Rejected alternatives:

- **Hash only, even for area names** — JOB would not wear aqua.
- **A unique color per theme** — the palette is eight slots.
- **Clients hash independently** — JS, Swift, and Lua would drift.

Evidence: `plan:202610/pomodoro_themes.md` PT5; epic decision `area_hues=area`;
`docs/pomodoro-themes.md`.

**Cost.** Recurring collisions need an explicit pin. Exempt keys such as GTD
are muted even when an area note shares the stem. Every client must wait for
Bob's `hue` field.

**Reopens when.** The palette grows, area notes stop being the hue source for
matching stems, or a client needs a hue before Bob can answer.

Superseded by [Theme Hue Is Config Then Pin Then Exempt Then Unconfigured Then Area Then Hash](#theme-hue-is-config-pin-exempt-area-hash), which
retires the pin-first order: a configured `themes:` color now wins over the
journal pin, and themes outside the configured vocabulary mute as
`unconfigured`.

## Theme Preferences Live In A Per-Host Journal {#theme-prefs-live-in-per-host-journal}

**Status:** Accepted

Hide, unhide, color, and rename events live in vault-synced `.bob/themes/<host>.jsonl`; fold is last-writer-wins and bob is the only writer.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, Bob Mac Capture, Obsidian plugins that hide, pin, or
rename themes.

**Claim.** Preferences live in `.bob/themes/<host>.jsonl`, one append-only file
per host inside the vault so Git syncs them. `host` is the same label
vault-sync uses in commit subjects. Events are `v: 1` `theme.hide`,
`theme.unhide`, `theme.color` (`hue` is a slot name or `null` to unpin), and
`theme.rename`. Fold reads every `*.jsonl` file, skips malformed lines with a
bounded warning, sorts by `(ts, host, path, line)`, and lets the last writer
win per key. A rename moves the source key's explicit state unless the target
already has state. bob is the only writer; other clients call bob.

**Why.** Frontmatter on daily notes would mix derived history with preferences.
A machine-local SQLite file would not sync hide/color across apollo and the
Mac. A single shared JSON file would lose concurrent host appends. Rejected
alternatives:

- **Daily-note frontmatter** — every hide would dirty today's ledger.
- **Machine-local SQLite** — hide on apollo would not reach the Mac.
- **One shared JSON object** — two hosts writing at once would clobber.

Evidence: `plan:202610/pomodoro_themes.md` PT4; `docs/pomodoro-themes.md`.

**Cost.** Fold must skip malformed lines. Rename is a logged event plus a
ledger rewrite, not a journal-only alias. Writers serialize through bob.

**Reopens when.** Concurrent host folds mis-order clocks often enough to need
a vector clock, or preferences must live outside the vault.

## Today Is Read From The Ledger, Never Written To Tasks {#today-is-read-from-the-ledger}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [READY Is Freshness-Gated With NEW and ROTTEN Review](#ready-is-freshness-gated)

Today is the open tasks with a dedicated Task Link under today's open Pomodoros, computed at read time by bob plan and bob-ledger-tools; never a tag, task-line field, or file-path filter; #now is retired.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault, dash.

**Claim.** Today means dedicated Task Links under today's **open** Pomodoros
only; closed 🍅 lines are history. The definition lives in `docs/plan.md`,
with Rust `today_tasks` and ledger-tools `isToday` sharing conformance
vectors. The dash sections are exclusive (TODAY / PENDING / NEXT / READY).
`#now` is removed everywhere, and "committed but not today" is the Next lane.

**Why.** A file-path filter selects tasks that live in the daily note (1
result against 7 live links), and a hooks-managed `#today` tag is a second
copy of the ledger rewritten on task lines every 15 minutes, with churn,
races, and staleness. `filter by function` can call the plugin api, and the
Tasks reload event exists. Rejected alternatives:

- **A path filter.** It measures residence, not work.
- **A `#today` tag.** A stopgap only, with write churn on every pass.
- **Keeping `#now` through its trial.** The trial already failed; the tag is
  retired now.
- **One `bob-dashboard` block.** The fallback if the Tasks refresh proves
  fragile.

Evidence:
`research:202609/retire_now_sticky_lanes_ledger_today/retire_now_sticky_lanes_ledger_today.md`;
epic `bob-cli-2y` (`plan:202609/retire_now_sticky_lanes.md`); phase
`bob-cli-2y.2` (superseding record).

**Cost.** It relies on an internal Tasks event. Headless `bob query` sees an
empty Today. There are two implementations (Rust and JavaScript) to keep in
sync. Resolver divergence on ambiguous basenames is documented. Capture can
no longer mark "this week" on new text.

**Reopens when.** Tasks removes the event or `app` access, or the refresh
proves unreliable.

Superseded in part by [READY Is Freshness-Gated With NEW and ROTTEN Review](#ready-is-freshness-gated) for the dash
section list only (TODAY → NEW → PENDING → NEXT → READY); the ledger-only
Today claim above is unchanged.

## Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked {#unblocked-tasks-are-offered}

**Status:** Accepted

Every would-be successor link from a managed Done gesture is offered for explicit selection; recovery remains automatic.

# Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked

*Requested · project*

aka successor offers, pull-in offers

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, Bob Mac Capture, vault.

**Claim.** Managed Done gestures keep recovery automatic: tasks still unblock, lose
`#prj_is_blocked`, and receive the `[unblocked::]` WRITE stamp when applicable, whether
or not anything is picked. Every would-be successor link is instead a
[Successor Offer](../reference/glossary.md#successor-offer): direct dependents (`hand_off`), open residents of a
recovered project (`project`), and project-finished pull-ins (`project_finished`). One
picker appears per gesture when offers exist; nothing is preselected and there is no
offer cap. Only picked rows are linked and raised to Next, receive a missing block ID,
and get `[fresh:: today]` (clearing `[unblocked::]` and `[keeps::]`). Unpicked rows
recover without a link and resurface through the existing freshness rules. `bob capture`
never prompts or auto-links: callers make an explicit selection, while the Mac presents
the choice in-panel and submits it to bob.

**Why.** A close once encountered eleven direct dependents and the all-or-nothing limit
linked none, leaving Bryan to hand-link selected tasks, including one in another
Pomodoro. A picker lets the person choose among all useful successors while retaining
automatic recovery and making project residents visible even when they are not direct
dependents. Project groups enumerate residents of the recovered project's note;
project-finished pull-ins retain their existing recovery and `#hide` removal, with the
link offered separately. The detailed contract is `docs/task-dependencies.md` §12 and
the accepted design is `plan:202610/successor_offers.md`.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Raise the cap.** Any finite cap still drops a valid fan-out, while an unbounded
automatic pass can plan too much work.
- **Auto-link direct dependents only.** It leaves project residents invisible and keeps
different successor classes inconsistent.
- **Skip the picker for one offer.** Even one candidate needs an explicit choice.
- **Choose after commit.** A later picker cannot reliably revalidate and atomically
apply the same gesture.
- **Use `>1,3` as the selection grammar.** Number and key selection is explicit in
capture; the UI owns its own multi-select interaction.
- **Put checkboxes in the Mac preview.** Choice is a distinct in-panel step, and bob
remains the sole capture and write authority.
- **Never prompt during the review walk.** A managed Done gesture has one consistent
offer choice, including when it began in the walk.
- **Use a tray of held offers.** Offers are tied to the close and are immediately
applied or left to recover; no separate queue is needed.

**Cost.** The Rust, cycler, navigation, and Mac surfaces must preserve one offer/key
contract. The picker pauses a managed Done gesture and each selected write must be
revalidated against current note text. Capture clients must understand additive offer
and pull-in output, and older Bob binaries need capability fallback in the Mac client.
Unpicked recovery continues to rely on the existing review tiers; no later rescue
command is included.

**Reopens when.** People need to retrieve offers after the gesture; offer sets become
too large for grouping and filtering; or a supported client cannot preserve the shared
selection and write contract.

Evidence: `plan:202610/successor_offers.md`; epic `bob-cli-7c` and phases
`bob-cli-7c.3`–`bob-cli-7c.7`; bob-cli `2d1adfa` (contract), `f5c82d6` (planner),
`e7a0c7b` (capture); Bob Mac Capture `6c4209b` (in-panel choice).

[Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers)

[Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](#projects-block-from-prj-line)

[Sub-projects Inherit Project Blocking](#subprojects-inherit-project-blocking)

[Bob Mac Capture Is A Thin Client Of bob](#mac-capture-is-a-thin-client)

## Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers {#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers}

**Status:** Superseded in part by [Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked](#unblocked-tasks-are-offered)

Every automatic Blocked-to-Ready recovery records [unblocked:: today] unless a WRITE skip applies, so the task is TICKLER in the next morning review; a keep on that row leaves the streak unchanged.

**Applies to.** bob-cli, bob-plugins, vault.

**Claim.** Every automatic transition of an open task from Blocked
`[?]` to Ready `[ ]` records `[unblocked:: today]` on the recovered
line (replacing any older value), unless a WRITE skip applies: the row
is outside freshness scope, has no `[fresh::]`, is already a scheduled
tickler (`fresh(t) < scheduled(t) ≤ today`), or lands in Next or
Pending. Writers are reconcile Unblock; capture/cycler close recovery
(including `project_member`); nav/cycler project recovery of
residents; and nav recoveries of lines other than the gesture's own
line. Every stamp clears the field; reconcile prunes `[unblocked:: U]`
when `fresh > U`. At read time,
`returned_on` is the latest of an arrived `scheduled` and a valid
`unblocked` (`fresh ≤ unblocked ≤ today`); `returned_by` is
`scheduled` or `unblocked`, with `scheduled` on a tie; RESURFACED plus
tier TICKLER follow from `returned_on`. A keep on a
`returned_by: unblocked` row neither increments nor resets
`[keeps::]`, and `decide_for` never opens the decision card for it.
`docs/freshness.md` §4 and §10b own the contract; see also
[Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](#review-walk-is-tiered) and
[READY Is Freshness-Gated With NEW and ROTTEN Review](#ready-is-freshness-gated).

**Why.** Recover-only, never-linked project members kept their old
`[fresh::]` and could sit FRESH, outside the walk, for up to six
mornings. Read-time `returned_on` from prerequisite completion dates
(option A) misses the project unblocks Bryan performs himself —
removing a `^prj` prerequisite or Ctrl+D of the project date — plus
deleted prerequisites and closed projects. Rejected alternatives:

- **Read-time `returned_on` (option A).** Misses those unblocks.
- **Clearing `[fresh::]`.** A stamp is a human confirmation; automation
  never stamps.
- **Recovering to Next.** That would invent a lane.
- **Successor-linking residents.** Residents recover recover-only.

Evidence:
`research:202610/unblocked_task_review_guarantee.md`;
`research:202610/prj_task_inline_schedule_and_deps.md` §4;
epic `bob-cli-6u` (`plan:202610/prj_line_project_blocking.md`);
bob-cli `f51ba28` (Rust freshness), `34d4ab6` (reconcile Unblock),
`13d183f` (close recovery);
bob-plugins `f47be84` (ledger-tools evaluator, `api.freshness` v12).

**Cost.** Automation writes a non-stamp freshness input. Recovery
writers live in four engines. The guarantee relies on reconcile having
run since the unblock. Lane walks must stay on. Old plugin versions do
not write the field during the mixed-version window; reconcile prunes
`fresh > U`.

**Reopens when.** A required surface cannot wait for reconcile, or
stamps must remain the only freshness write.

Superseded in part: project residents are now offered as successors and linked only
when picked; the former rejected "successor-linking residents" behavior is an explicit
offer. See [Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked](#unblocked-tasks-are-offered).
